title.zh: 卷一百五十一 志第一百〇四 輿服三
title.raw: 卷一百五十一 志第一百〇四 輿服三 Volume 151 Treatises 104: Carriages and Clothes 3

sentences.zh: 輿服三○天子之服皇太子附後妃之服命婦附

translations.literal: Carriages and Clothes 3 ○ Imperial Robes, with appendix on the Crown Prince; Appendix on Empresses and Consorts; Appendix on Ennobled Ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Carriages and Clothes 3 — Imperial Robes, with an appendix on the crown prince; appendices on empresses and consorts, and on ennobled ladies.

sentences.zh: 天子之服，一曰大裘冕，二曰袞冕，三曰通天冠，絳紗袍，四曰履袍，五曰衫袍，六曰窄袍，天子祀享、朝會、親耕及親事、燕居之服也，七曰禦閱服，天子之戎服也。

translations.literal: The emperor's robes: first, the great fur robe and coronet; second, the embroidered sacrificial robe and coronet; third, the heaven-penetrating cap with deep-red gauze robe; fourth, the footed robe; fifth, the open robe; sixth, the narrow robe—these are the emperor's garments for sacrifices, court assemblies, plowing the sacred field, wedding rites, and daily leisure; seventh, the review attire, the emperor's military garb.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had seven sets of regalia: the great fur robe and coronet; the embroidered sacrificial robe and coronet; the heaven-penetrating cap with deep-red gauze robe; the footed robe, open robe, and narrow robe for sacrifices, court, the sacred plowing, weddings, and everyday wear; and finally the review dress, his military attire.

sentences.zh: 中興之後則有之。

translations.literal: These existed only after the Restoration.
translations.idiomatic: These categories were established only after the dynastic restoration.

sentences.zh: 大裘之製。

translations.literal: The design of the great fur robe.
translations.idiomatic: The great fur robe.

sentences.zh: 神宗元豐四年，詳定郊廟奉祀禮文所言：“《周禮·司裘》‘掌為大裘，以供王祀天之服’；

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanfeng under Emperor Shenzong, the commission for ritual texts on suburban and temple sacrifices stated: "The Rites of Zhou, Director of Furs: 'He is charged with making the great fur robe to supply the king's garment for sacrificing to Heaven'";
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanfeng (1081), the commission revising suburban and temple ritual texts cited the Rites of Zhou: the Director of Furs "prepares the great fur robe as the king's dress for Heaven worship."

sentences.zh: 《司服》‘王祀昊天上帝，則服大裘而冕，祀五帝亦如之。

translations.literal: The Director of Robes: 'When the king sacrifices to the August Heaven, he wears the great fur robe and coronet; when sacrificing to the Five Emperors, it is likewise.'
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Robes adds that when the king worships the August Heaven, he wears the great fur robe and coronet, and does the same when sacrificing to the Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 享先王則袞冕’。

translations.literal: When offering to former kings, he wears the embroidered robe and coronet.'
translations.idiomatic: For offerings to the royal ancestors, he wears the embroidered robe and coronet instead.

sentences.zh: 而《禮記》云：‘郊祭之日，王被袞以象天，戴冕璪十有二旒，則天數也。

translations.literal: Yet the Book of Rites says: 'On the day of the suburban sacrifice, the king dons the embroidered robe to symbolize Heaven, and wears a coronet with twelve pendants of jade beads—the number of Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites, however, says that on the day of the suburban rite the king puts on the embroidered robe to represent Heaven and wears a coronet with twelve jade pendants, matching the number of Heaven.

sentences.zh: ’王肅據《家語》，以為臨燔柴，脫袞冕，著大裘。

translations.literal: ' Wang Su, relying on the Family Sayings, held that when approaching the kindling of the firewood, one removes the embroidered robe and coronet and puts on the great fur robe.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su, citing the Family Sayings, argued that at the moment of kindling the sacrificial fire the king should remove the embroidered robe and coronet and don the great fur robe.

sentences.zh: 則是《禮記》被袞，與《周禮》大裘，郊祀並用二服，事不相戾，但服之有先後耳。

translations.literal: Thus the Book of Rites' donning of the embroidered robe and the Rites of Zhou's great fur robe are both used in the suburban sacrifice; the two are not contradictory, but only differ in the order in which the garments are worn.
translations.idiomatic: So the embroidered robe in the Book of Rites and the great fur robe in the Rites of Zhou both belong to the same suburban rite; the texts do not conflict, but prescribe different garments at different stages.

sentences.zh: 是以《開寶通禮》：皇帝服袞冕出赴行宮，祀日，服袞冕至大次；

translations.literal: Therefore the Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao: the emperor wears the embroidered robe and coronet when departing for the temporary palace; on the day of sacrifice, he wears the embroidered robe and coronet until reaching the great side-tent;
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao accordingly had the emperor wear the embroidered robe and coronet when leaving for the suburban lodge, and again on the sacrifice day until he reached the great side-tent;

sentences.zh: 質明，改服大裘而冕出次。

translations.literal: at dawn, he changes into the great fur robe and coronet and emerges from the tent.
translations.idiomatic: at dawn he would change into the great fur robe and coronet before leaving the tent.

sentences.zh: 蓋袞冕盛服而文之備者，故於郊之前期被之，以至大次。

translations.literal: For the embroidered robe and coronet are the full ceremonial dress with complete ornament, and so are donned in the period before the suburban rite, until reaching the great side-tent.
translations.idiomatic: The embroidered robe and coronet were the full ceremonial regalia, worn in the preparatory phase of the suburban rite up to the side-tent.

sentences.zh: 既臨燔柴，則脫袞冕服裘，以明天道至質，故被裘以體之。

translations.literal: Once one approaches the kindling of the firewood, one removes the embroidered robe and coronet and wears the fur robe, to manifest that the Way of Heaven is utterly plain; therefore one dons the fur robe to embody this.
translations.idiomatic: At the kindling of the fire he would remove the embroidered robe and coronet and wear the fur robe, showing that Heaven's way is utterly plain—and so he embodied that plainness in fur.

sentences.zh: 今儀注，車駕赴青城，服通天冠、絳紗袍。

translations.literal: The present ritual directives have the imperial carriage proceed to Qingcheng wearing the heaven-penetrating cap and deep-red gauze robe.
translations.idiomatic: Under current ritual instructions, the emperor travels to Qingcheng in the heaven-penetrating cap and deep-red gauze robe.

sentences.zh: 祀之日，乃服靴袍至大次，服袞冕臨祭，非尚質之義。

translations.literal: On the day of sacrifice, he wears boots and robe to the great side-tent and the embroidered robe and coronet when approaching the sacrifice—this is not the meaning of honoring plainness.
translations.idiomatic: On the sacrifice day he wears boots and robe to the side-tent and the embroidered robe and coronet at the altar—contrary to the principle of plainness.

sentences.zh: 乞並依《開寶通禮》。”

translations.literal: We beg that all be done according to the Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that practice be brought fully into line with the Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao."

sentences.zh: 詔詳定所參議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the commission to deliberate further.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the revision commission to deliberate further.

sentences.zh: 又言：“臣等詳大裘之製，本以尚質，而後世反以尚文，故冕之飾大為不經。

translations.literal: They also stated: "We have examined in detail the design of the great fur robe, which was originally meant to honor plainness, yet later ages turned instead to honoring ornament, so the coronet's decoration became greatly improper.
translations.idiomatic: They added: "We find that the great fur robe was meant to honor plainness, but later ages prized ornament instead, so coronet decoration grew wildly improper.

sentences.zh: 而禮書所載，上有垂旒加飾，又異‘大裘不裼’之說。

translations.literal: Yet what the ritual books record has hanging pendants and added ornament on top, which again differs from the saying 'the great fur robe is not worn open.'
translations.idiomatic: Ritual texts describe pendants and added ornament, which conflicts with the rule that the great fur robe is not worn open.

sentences.zh: 今參考諸說，大裘冕無旒，廣八寸，長一尺六寸，前圜後方，前低寸二分，玄表朱裏，以繒為之。

translations.literal: Now, consulting the various accounts, the great fur coronet has no pendants, is eight inches wide and one foot six inches long, round in front and square behind, the front one inch and two tenths lower; black on the outside and vermilion within, made of silk.
translations.idiomatic: We propose, after weighing the sources, a great fur coronet without pendants, eight inches wide and one foot six long, round in front and square behind, the front edge one and two-tenths inches lower, black outside and vermilion within, of silk.

sentences.zh: 玉笄以朱組為紘，玉瑱以玄紞垂之。

translations.literal: A jade hairpin with vermilion cord as the chin strap; jade earplugs with black cord hanging from them.
translations.idiomatic: A jade pin with vermilion chin strap, and jade earplugs suspended on black cord.

sentences.zh: 為裘以黑羔皮，領袖以黑繒，纁裳朱紘而無章飾。

translations.literal: The robe is made of black lamb fur, collar and sleeves of black silk, with a light-red skirt and vermilion sash and no patterned ornament.
translations.idiomatic: The robe itself is black lamb fur, with black silk collar and sleeves, a light-red skirt and vermilion sash, and no emblems.

sentences.zh: 佩白玉，玄組綬。

translations.literal: He wears white jade, with a black cord sash.
translations.idiomatic: White jade is worn on a black cord sash.

sentences.zh: 革帶，博二寸，玉鉤䚢，以佩紘屬之。

translations.literal: A leather belt two inches wide, with jade hook and plaque, to which the sash pendant is attached.
translations.idiomatic: A two-inch leather belt with jade hook and plaque, from which the sash pendant hangs.

sentences.zh: 素帶，朱裏，絳純其外，上朱下綠。

translations.literal: A plain belt, vermilion within, with deep-red edging on the outside, vermilion above and green below.
translations.idiomatic: A plain belt lined in vermilion, edged in deep red, vermilion above and green below.

sentences.zh: 白紗中單，皂領，青褾、襈、裾。

translations.literal: A white gauze inner robe, black collar, with green border, facing, and hem.
translations.idiomatic: A white gauze under-robe with black collar and green trim, facing, and hem.

sentences.zh: 朱襪，赤舄，黑絇、繶、純。

translations.literal: Vermilion socks, red shoes, with black laces, welts, and edging.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion socks and red shoes with black laces, welts, and edging.

sentences.zh: 乞下所屬製造。

translations.literal: We beg that orders be sent down to the relevant offices to manufacture these.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the appropriate offices be ordered to make them.

sentences.zh: 其當暑奉祠之服，乞降梁陸瑋議以黑繒為裘，及《唐·輿服志》以黑羔皮為緣。”

translations.literal: As for the summer sacrificial garment, we beg to adopt Lu Wei of Liang's proposal to use black silk for the fur robe, and the Tang Carriages and Clothes Treatise's use of black lamb fur for the border."
translations.idiomatic: For summer sacrifices, we ask to follow Lu Wei of Liang in using black silk for the robe and the Tang treatise in edging it with black lamb fur."

sentences.zh: 詔重詳定。

translations.literal: An edict ordered further detailed revision.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered another round of detailed revision.

sentences.zh: 光祿寺丞、集賢校理陸佃言：“臣詳冕服有六。

translations.literal: Lu Dian, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, stated: "Your servant finds that there are six coronet-robes.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dian of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and the Hall of Assembled Worthies reported: "I find six types of coronet-robes.

sentences.zh: 《周官》弁師雲‘掌王之五冕’，則大裘與袞同冕。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou, Cap-Master, says 'he is in charge of the king's five coronets,' so the great fur robe shares a coronet with the embroidered robe.
translations.idiomatic: The Cap-Master in the Offices of Zhou oversees the king's five coronets, which means the great fur robe shares its coronet with the embroidered robe.

sentences.zh: 故《禮記》雲‘郊之日，王被袞以象天’。

translations.literal: Hence the Book of Rites says 'on the day of the suburban sacrifice, the king dons the embroidered robe to symbolize Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Book of Rites: on the suburban day the king dons the embroidered robe to symbolize Heaven.

sentences.zh: 又曰‘服之襲也，充，美也’；

translations.literal: It also says 'to wear a garment as an outer layer is to fill it out, to beautify it';
translations.idiomatic: It also says that wearing a garment as an outer layer is to complete and adorn it;

sentences.zh: ‘禮不盛，服不充，故大裘不裼’。

translations.literal: 'When the rite is not grand, the garment is not filled out; therefore the great fur robe is not worn open.'
translations.idiomatic: "when the rite is not grand the garment is not layered; therefore the great fur robe is not worn open."

sentences.zh: 此明王服大裘，以袞衣襲之也。

translations.literal: This makes clear that the king wears the great fur robe with the embroidered garment as its outer layer.
translations.idiomatic: This shows the king wore the great fur robe with the embroidered garment as its outer layer.

sentences.zh: 先儒或謂周祀天地皆服大裘，而大裘之冕無旒，非是。

translations.literal: Earlier scholars held that in Zhou sacrifices to Heaven and Earth one always wore the great fur robe, and that the great fur coronet had no pendants—this is incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: Some earlier scholars claimed Zhou sacrifices to Heaven and Earth always used the great fur robe and that its coronet had no pendants—but that is wrong.

sentences.zh: 蓋古者裘不徒服，其上必皆有衣，故曰‘緇衣羔裘’，‘黃衣狐裘’，‘素衣麑裘’。

translations.literal: For in antiquity a fur robe was never worn alone; there was always a garment over it, hence 'black garment with lamb fur,' 'yellow garment with fox fur,' 'white garment with fawn fur.'
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity fur was never worn alone; a garment always went over it—hence "black robe with lamb fur," "yellow robe with fox fur," and "white robe with fawn fur."

sentences.zh: 如郊祀徒服大裘，則是表裘以見天地。

translations.literal: If in the suburban sacrifice one wore only the great fur robe, that would be presenting the outer fur to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: If the suburban rite used only the great fur robe, one would be presenting the outer fur directly to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 表裘不入公門，而乃欲以見天地，可乎？

translations.literal: An outer fur may not enter the public gate—yet one would wish to present it to Heaven and Earth; is that permissible?
translations.idiomatic: Outer fur was not admitted through the public gate—how then could it be shown to Heaven and Earth?

sentences.zh: 且先王之服，冬裘夏葛以適寒暑，未有能易之者也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the former kings' garments were fur in winter and ramie in summer to suit cold and heat; none could simply exchange them.
translations.idiomatic: The former kings wore fur in winter and ramie in summer to suit the seasons; no one could simply swap them at will.

sentences.zh: 郊祀天地，有裘無袞，則夏祀赤帝與至日祭地祇，亦將被裘乎？

translations.literal: If suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth had fur but no embroidered robe, then in summer sacrifices to the Red Emperor and the solstice sacrifice to the Earth Spirit, would one also don fur?
translations.idiomatic: If suburban rites used fur without the embroidered robe, would summer sacrifices to the Red Emperor and the solstice rite to Earth also require fur?

sentences.zh: 然則王者冬祀昊天上帝，中裘而表袞，明矣。

translations.literal: Thus when the king in winter sacrifices to the August Heaven, fur within and embroidered robe without is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly, in winter the king sacrificed to the August Heaven with fur within and the embroidered robe without.

sentences.zh: 至於夏祀天神地祇，則去裘服袞，以順時序。

translations.literal: As for summer sacrifices to the spirits of Heaven and Earth, one removes the fur and wears the embroidered robe, to accord with the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: In summer sacrifices to Heaven and Earth he removed the fur and wore the embroidered robe, following the season.

sentences.zh: 《周官》曰‘凡四時之祭祀，以宜服之’，明夏不必衣裘也。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou says 'for all seasonal sacrifices, wear what is appropriate'—making clear that in summer one need not wear fur.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou says sacrifices in every season require appropriate dress—so summer did not require fur.

sentences.zh: 或曰，祭天尚質，故徒服大裘，被袞則非尚質。

translations.literal: Some say that in sacrificing to Heaven one honors plainness, and therefore wears only the great fur robe; to don the embroidered robe is not honoring plainness.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that Heaven worship honors plainness, so only the great fur robe should be worn and the embroidered robe would violate that principle.

sentences.zh: 臣以為尚質者，明有所尚而已，不皆用質也。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that honoring plainness means making clear what is honored; one does not use plainness in every respect.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that honoring plainness means marking what is primary—not using plain materials in every detail.

sentences.zh: 今欲冬至禋祀昊天上帝，服裘被袞，其餘祀天及祀地祇，並請服袞去裘，各以其宜服之。”

translations.literal: Now we wish that at the winter solstice suburban sacrifice to the August Heaven, one wear fur with the embroidered robe as outer layer; for all other sacrifices to Heaven and to the Earth Spirit, we beg to wear the embroidered robe and remove the fur, each according to what is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: We propose that at the winter solstice suburban rite to the August Heaven the king wear fur under the embroidered robe, and that all other sacrifices to Heaven and Earth use the embroidered robe without fur, each as the season requires."

sentences.zh: 於是詳定所言：“裘不可徒服。

translations.literal: Thereupon the revision commission stated: "A fur robe may not be worn alone.
translations.idiomatic: The revision commission then ruled: "Fur may not be worn alone.

sentences.zh: 《禮記》曰‘大裘不裼’，則襲可知，所謂大裘之襲者，袞也，與袞同冕。

translations.literal: The Book of Rites says 'the great fur robe is not worn open,' from which the outer layer may be inferred; what is called the outer layer of the great fur robe is the embroidered garment, sharing the coronet with the embroidered robe.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says the great fur robe is not worn open, which implies an outer layer—the embroidered garment, sharing the same coronet.

sentences.zh: 伏請冬祀昊天與黑帝，皆服大裘，被以袞。

translations.literal: We humbly beg that in winter sacrifices to the August Heaven and the Black Emperor, one wear the great fur robe with the embroidered robe as outer layer.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that winter sacrifices to the August Heaven and the Black Emperor use the great fur robe under the embroidered garment.

sentences.zh: 其餘非冬祀天及夏至祭地，則皆服袞。”

translations.literal: For all other sacrifices that are not winter sacrifices to Heaven or the summer solstice sacrifice to Earth, one wears only the embroidered robe.
translations.idiomatic: All other rites—except winter Heaven worship and the summer solstice Earth sacrifice—should use only the embroidered robe."

sentences.zh: 六年，尚書禮部言：“經有大裘而無其製，近世所為，惟梁、隋、唐為可考。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Ministry of Rites of the Department of State Affairs stated: "The classics mention the great fur robe but not its design; what recent ages have made can be checked only against Liang, Sui, and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Ministry of Rites reported: "The classics name the great fur robe but not its design; only Liang, Sui, and Tang practice can be consulted.

sentences.zh: 請緣隋製，以黑羔皮為裘，黑繒為領袖及裏、緣，袂廣可運肘，長可蔽膝。

translations.literal: We beg to follow the Sui design, using black lamb fur for the robe, black silk for collar, sleeves, lining, and border; sleeves wide enough to move the elbows, length enough to cover the knees.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to follow Sui practice: black lamb fur for the robe, black silk for collar, sleeves, lining, and trim; sleeves wide enough for the elbows, length to the knee.

sentences.zh: 按皇侃說，祭服之下有袍繭，袍繭之下有中衣。

translations.literal: According to Huang Kan's explanation, beneath the sacrificial garment is the padded robe, and beneath the padded robe is the inner garment.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Kan held that beneath the sacrificial garment came a padded robe, and beneath that the inner garment.

sentences.zh: 朝服，裼衣之下有裘，裘之下有中衣。

translations.literal: For court dress, beneath the open garment is fur, and beneath the fur is the inner garment.
translations.idiomatic: For court dress, fur lay beneath the open outer garment, with the inner garment beneath the fur.

sentences.zh: 然則今之親郊，中單當在大裘之下，其袂之廣狹，衣之長短，皆當如裘。

translations.literal: Thus for the present emperor's personal suburban sacrifice, the inner robe should lie beneath the great fur robe; the width of its sleeves and the length of the garment should all match the fur robe.
translations.idiomatic: For the emperor's personal suburban rite, the inner robe should lie under the great fur robe, matching it in sleeve width and length.

sentences.zh: 伏乞改製。”

translations.literal: We humbly beg that the design be altered."
translations.idiomatic: We humbly ask that the design be revised."

sentences.zh: 於是神宗始服大裘，而加袞冕焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Emperor Shenzong first wore the great fur robe, with the embroidered robe and coronet added over it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong then first wore the great fur robe with the embroidered robe and coronet over it.

sentences.zh: 哲宗元祐元年，禮部言：“元豐所造大裘，雖用黑羔皮，乃作短袍樣，襲於袞衣之下，仍與袞服同冕，未合典禮。”

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou under Emperor Zhezong, the Ministry of Rites stated: "The great fur robe made in Yuanfeng, though using black lamb fur, was fashioned like a short coat and worn as an inner layer beneath the embroidered garment, still sharing the coronet with the embroidered robe—this does not accord with canonical ritual."
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 1 (1086) the Ministry of Rites said the Yuanfeng great fur robe, though of black lamb fur, was cut like a short coat worn under the embroidered garment and shared its coronet—contrary to canonical ritual.

sentences.zh: 下禮部、太常寺共議。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for joint deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The case was sent to the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for joint deliberation.

sentences.zh: 上官均、吳安詩、常安民、劉唐老、襲原、姚勔請依元豐新禮，丁騭請循祖宗故事，王愈請仿唐製，朱光庭、周秩請以玄衣襲裘。

translations.literal: Shangguan Jun, Wu Anshi, Chang Anmin, Liu Tanglao, Xi Yuan, and Yao Peng asked to follow the new rites of Yuanfeng; Ding E asked to follow the precedents of the imperial ancestors; Wang Yu asked to imitate Tang practice; Zhu Guangting and Zhou Zhi asked to use a black garment as the outer layer over fur.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Jun, Wu Anshi, Chang Anmin, Liu Tanglao, Xi Yuan, and Yao Peng favored the Yuanfeng rites; Ding E the ancestral precedents; Wang Yu Tang practice; Zhu Guangting and Zhou Zhi a black outer garment over fur.

sentences.zh: 獨禮部員外郎何洵直在元豐中嚐預詳定，以陸佃所議有可疑者八：

translations.literal: Only He Xunzhi, Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites, who in Yuanfeng had taken part in the detailed revision, found eight doubtful points in Lu Dian's proposals:
translations.idiomatic: He Xunzhi of the Ministry of Rites, who had served on the Yuanfeng revision, alone raised eight objections to Lu Dian's proposals:

sentences.zh: 按《周禮·節服氏》“掌祭祀朝覲，袞冕六人，惟王之太常”；

translations.literal: According to the Rites of Zhou, Master of Regalia: "In charge of sacrifices and audiences, six men in embroidered robes and coronets—for the king's great banner alone";
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou, Master of Regalia, assigns six attendants in embroidered robe and coronet for the king's great banner at sacrifices and audiences;

sentences.zh: “郊祀，裘冕二人”。

translations.literal: "For suburban sacrifice, two men in fur robe and coronet."
translations.idiomatic: "and two in fur robe and coronet for suburban sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 既雲袞冕，又雲裘冕，是袞與裘各有冕。

translations.literal: Since it speaks of both embroidered robe and coronet and fur robe and coronet, embroidered robe and fur each have their own coronet.
translations.idiomatic: Because both embroidered and fur coronets are named, each garment had its own coronet.

sentences.zh: 乃雲裘與袞同冕，當以袞襲之。

translations.literal: Yet Lu Dian says fur and embroidered robe share a coronet and that the embroidered robe should be the outer layer—
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lu Dian claims they shared one coronet and that the embroidered robe should be the outer layer—

sentences.zh: 裘既無冕，又襲於袞，中裘而表袞，何以示裘袞之別哉？

translations.literal: if fur has no coronet of its own and is worn as an inner layer under the embroidered robe, fur within and embroidered without—how can the distinction between fur and embroidered robe be shown?
translations.idiomatic: if fur had no coronet and lay under the embroidered robe, how could fur and embroidered dress be distinguished?

sentences.zh: 古人雖質，不應以裘為夏服，蓋冬用大裘，當暑則以同色繒為之。

translations.literal: The ancients, though plain, would not have used fur as summer dress; in winter they used the great fur robe, and in hot weather made it of silk in the same color.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients, though plain, would not wear fur in summer; in winter they used the great fur robe, and in heat substituted silk of the same color.

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：“郊祭之日，王被袞以象天。”

translations.literal: The Record says: "On the day of the suburban sacrifice, the king dons the embroidered robe to symbolize Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "On the suburban sacrifice day the king dons the embroidered robe to symbolize Heaven."

sentences.zh: 若謂裘上被袞，以被為襲，則《家語》亦有“被裘象天”之文。

translations.literal: If one holds that the embroidered robe is put on over fur and that 'donning' means 'outer layer,' then the Family Sayings also has the phrase 'donning fur to symbolize Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: If layering the embroidered robe over fur counts as 'donning,' the Family Sayings also speaks of 'donning fur to symbolize Heaven.'

sentences.zh: 諸儒或言“臨燔柴，脫袞冕，著大裘”，或云“脫裘服袞”，蓋裘袞無同冕兼服之理。

translations.literal: Various scholars say either 'when approaching the kindling, remove embroidered robe and coronet and put on the great fur robe' or 'remove fur and wear the embroidered robe'—for fur and embroidered robe have no principle of sharing one coronet and wearing both together.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars say either remove the embroidered robe and coronet for the great fur robe at the kindling, or remove fur for the embroidered robe—fur and embroidered dress cannot share one coronet and be worn together.

sentences.zh: 今乃以二服合為一，可乎？

translations.literal: To combine the two garments into one now—can that be right?
translations.idiomatic: Can the two garments rightly be merged into one?

sentences.zh: 且大裘，天子吉服之最上，若大圭、大路之比，是裘之在表者。

translations.literal: Moreover, the great fur robe is the highest of the emperor's auspicious garments, comparable to the great scepter and great chariot—it is fur worn as the outer layer.
translations.idiomatic: The great fur robe was the highest of the emperor's auspicious garments, like the great scepter and great chariot—fur worn outward.

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：“大裘不裼。”

translations.literal: The Record says: "The great fur robe is not worn open."
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "The great fur robe is not worn open."

sentences.zh: 說者曰，無別衣以裼之，蓋他服之裘褻，故表裘不入公門。

translations.literal: Expositors say there is no other garment to wear it open over it; other garments' fur is inner, hence outer fur does not enter the public gate.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators explain that no other garment was worn open over it; ordinary fur was inner dress, so outer fur did not pass the public gate.

sentences.zh: 事天以報本復始，故露質見素，不為表襮，而冕亦無旒，何必假他衣以藩飾之乎？

translations.literal: In serving Heaven to repay the root and renew the beginning, one therefore shows plain substance and simplicity, makes no outer display, and the coronet too has no pendants—why borrow another garment to screen and adorn it?
translations.idiomatic: Serving Heaven to repay the origin and renew the year required plain substance—no outer display, no coronet pendants—so why borrow another garment to adorn it?

sentences.zh: 凡裘上有衣謂之裼，裼上有衣謂之襲，襲者，裘上重二衣也。

translations.literal: Whenever there is a garment over fur it is called 'open'; when there is a garment over the open garment it is called 'outer layer'; an outer layer means two garments over the fur.
translations.idiomatic: A garment over fur is 'open' dress; a garment over that is an 'outer layer'—two garments above the fur.

sentences.zh: 大裘本不裼，《鄭志》乃云：“裘上有玄衣，與裘同色。”

translations.literal: The great fur robe by nature is not worn open; yet the Zheng Records say: "Over the fur is a black garment of the same color as the fur."
translations.idiomatic: The great fur robe was not worn open, yet the Zheng Records claim a black garment of the same color lay over the fur.

sentences.zh: 蓋趙商之徒，附會為說，不與經合。

translations.literal: This was likely forced interpretation by Zhao Shang and his followers, not in accord with the classics.
translations.idiomatic: That was likely a forced reading by Zhao Shang and others, not supported by the classics.

sentences.zh: 襲之為義，本出於重遝，非一衣也。

translations.literal: The meaning of 'outer layer' originally comes from layering, not a single garment.
translations.idiomatic: An 'outer layer' originally meant true layering, not a single over-garment.

sentences.zh: 古者齋祭異冠，齋服降祭服一等。

translations.literal: In antiquity fasting and sacrifice used different caps; fasting dress was one rank below sacrificial dress.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity fasting and sacrifice used different headgear; fasting dress ranked one degree below sacrificial dress.

sentences.zh: 祀昊天上帝、五帝，以裘冕祭，則袞冕齋。

translations.literal: In sacrificing to the August Heaven and the Five Emperors, one sacrifices in fur robe and coronet, and fasts in embroidered robe and coronet.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to the August Heaven and the Five Emperors used the fur coronet; fasting used the embroidered coronet.

sentences.zh: 故鄭氏云：“王齋服袞冕。”

translations.literal: Hence Master Zheng says: "The king fasts in embroidered robe and coronet."
translations.idiomatic: Master Zheng therefore says: "The king fasts in embroidered robe and coronet."

sentences.zh: 是袞冕者，祀天之齋服也。

translations.literal: Thus the embroidered robe and coronet are the fasting dress for sacrificing to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The embroidered robe and coronet were therefore the fasting dress for Heaven worship.

sentences.zh: 唐《開元》及《開寶禮》始以袞冕為齋服，裘冕為祭服，兼與張融“臨燔柴脫袞服裘”之義合。

translations.literal: Only in the Tang Kaiyuan Rites and the Kaibao Rites did the embroidered robe and coronet become fasting dress and the fur robe and coronet sacrificial dress, which also agrees with Zhang Rong's meaning of 'when approaching the kindling, remove the embroidered robe and wear fur.'
translations.idiomatic: Only under the Tang Kaiyuan and Song Kaibao rites did the embroidered coronet become fasting dress and the fur coronet sacrificial dress—matching Zhang Rong's rule to remove the embroidered robe for fur at the kindling.

sentences.zh: 請從唐製，兼改製大裘，以黑繒為之。

translations.literal: We beg to follow Tang practice and also revise the great fur robe, making it of black silk.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to follow Tang practice and remake the great fur robe in black silk.

sentences.zh: 佃復破其說曰：

translations.literal: Lu Dian in turn refuted his arguments, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dian rebutted him as follows:

sentences.zh: 夫大裘而冕，謂之裘冕，非大裘而冕，謂之袞冕。

translations.literal: When one wears the great fur robe with a coronet, it is called fur robe and coronet; when one does not wear the great fur robe with a coronet, it is called embroidered robe and coronet.
translations.idiomatic: The great fur robe with coronet is the fur coronet; any other coronet dress is the embroidered coronet.

sentences.zh: 則裘冕必服袞，袞冕不必服裘。

translations.literal: Thus when in fur robe and coronet one must wear the embroidered garment; when in embroidered robe and coronet one need not wear fur.
translations.idiomatic: The fur coronet therefore requires the embroidered garment underneath; the embroidered coronet does not require fur.

sentences.zh: 今特言裘冕者，主冬至言之。

translations.literal: The reason fur robe and coronet is mentioned specifically now is that the discussion chiefly concerns the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Fur coronet is singled out here chiefly with the winter solstice in mind.

sentences.zh: 《周禮·司裘》：“掌為大裘，以供王祀天之服。”

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou, Director of Furs: "He is charged with making the great fur robe to supply the king's garment for sacrificing to Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Furs prepares the great fur robe as the king's dress for Heaven worship.

sentences.zh: 則祀地不服大裘，以夏日至，不可服裘故也。

translations.literal: Thus in sacrificing to Earth one does not wear the great fur robe, because at the summer solstice one cannot wear fur.
translations.idiomatic: Earth sacrifice therefore omits the great fur robe, since fur cannot be worn at the summer solstice.

sentences.zh: 今謂大裘當暑，以同色繒為之，尤不經見。

translations.literal: To say now that in hot weather the great fur robe should be made of silk in the same color is especially absurd.
translations.idiomatic: The notion of substituting same-colored silk for fur in summer heat is especially absurd.

sentences.zh: 兼裼襲，一衣而已，初無重遝之義。

translations.literal: As for combining 'open' and 'outer layer,' it is a single garment; originally there was no meaning of layering.
translations.idiomatic: As for open dress and outer layer, these concern a single garment, not true layering.

sentences.zh: 被裘而覆之則曰襲，袒而露裘之美則曰裼。

translations.literal: When fur is covered over it is called 'outer layer'; when the fur's beauty is bared by opening the garment it is called 'open.'
translations.idiomatic: Covering the fur is an outer layer; baring the fur's beauty is open dress.

sentences.zh: 所謂“大裘不裼”，則非袞而何？

translations.literal: What is meant by 'the great fur robe is not worn open'—if not the embroidered robe, then what?
translations.idiomatic: If the great fur robe is 'not worn open,' what can that mean except the embroidered robe as cover?

sentences.zh: 《玉藻》曰：“禮不盛，服不充，故大裘不裼。”

translations.literal: The Jade Recordings says: "When the rite is not grand, the garment is not filled out, therefore the great fur robe is not worn open."
translations.idiomatic: The Jade Recordings says that when the rite is not grand the garment is not completed, so the great fur robe is not worn open.

sentences.zh: 則明不裼而襲也，充，美也。

translations.literal: This makes clear that one does not wear it open but as an outer layer; "filled out" means "adorned."
translations.idiomatic: This shows one does not wear it open but as an outer layer; "filled out" means adorned.

sentences.zh: 鄭氏謂大裘之上有玄衣，雖不知覆裘以袞，然尚知大裘不可徒服，必有玄衣以覆之。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says that above the great fur robe there is a dark garment; although he did not know to cover the fur with the embroidered robe, he still knew the great fur robe could not be worn alone and that there must be a dark garment to cover it.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan held that a dark garment went over the great fur robe; though he did not identify the cover as the embroidered robe, he still knew the great fur robe could not be worn alone and required a covering garment.

sentences.zh: 《玉藻》有屍襲之義。

translations.literal: The Jade Recordings has the meaning of "outer layer for the corpse."
translations.idiomatic: The Jade Recordings describes the outer layer worn on the corpse.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》裘冕注云：“裘冕者，從屍服也。”

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou annotation on the fur coronet says: "The fur coronet follows the corpse's dress."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou gloss on the fur coronet says the fur coronet follows the corpse's dress.

sentences.zh: 夫屍服大裘而襲，則王服大裘而襲可知。

translations.literal: Since the corpse wears the great fur robe with an outer layer, it may be inferred that the king wears the great fur robe with an outer layer.
translations.idiomatic: If the corpse wore the great fur robe with an outer layer, the king must have done the same.

sentences.zh: 且裘不可以徒服，故被以袞，豈借袞以為飾哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, fur cannot be worn alone, therefore it is covered with the embroidered robe—how could one borrow the embroidered robe merely as ornament?
translations.idiomatic: Fur cannot be worn alone, so it is covered with the embroidered robe—not as mere ornament.

sentences.zh: 今謂祭天用袞冕為齋服，裘冕為祭服，此乃襲先儒之謬誤。

translations.literal: Now some say that for sacrificing to Heaven the embroidered robe and coronet are fasting dress, and the fur coronet is sacrificial dress—this merely repeats the errors of earlier scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Calling the embroidered robe and coronet fasting dress and the fur coronet sacrificial dress for Heaven worship merely repeats earlier scholars' mistakes.

sentences.zh: 後漢顯宗初服日、月、星辰十二章，以祀天地。

translations.literal: At the start of Later Han Emperor Ming's reign, he wore the twelve emblems of sun, moon, and stars to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign in Later Han, he wore the twelve emblem pattern of sun, moon, and stars when sacrificing to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 自魏以來，皆用袞服。

translations.literal: From Wei onward, all used the embroidered robe.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wei dynasty onward, the embroidered robe was always used.

sentences.zh: 則漢、魏祭天，嚐服袞矣，雖無大裘，未能盡合於禮，固未嚐有表裘而祭者也。

translations.literal: Thus Han and Wei sacrifices to Heaven always wore the embroidered robe; although without the great fur robe they could not fully conform to ritual, they never wore outer fur to sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei Heaven sacrifices always used the embroidered robe; lacking the great fur robe they did not fully match the rites, yet they never sacrificed in outer fur alone.

sentences.zh: 且裘，內服也，與袍同。

translations.literal: Moreover, fur is an inner garment, the same as a robe.
translations.idiomatic: Fur is an inner garment, like an ordinary robe.

sentences.zh: 袍褻矣，而欲襌以祭天，以明示質，是欲衤義衣以見上帝也。

translations.literal: A robe is already intimate dress, yet one wishes to wear a thin unlined garment to sacrifice to Heaven, plainly showing substance—this is like wishing to wear undergarments to appear before the Supreme God.
translations.idiomatic: A robe is already intimate dress; to sacrifice to Heaven in only a thin unlined robe, openly displaying plain substance, would be like appearing before the Supreme God in one's undergarments.

sentences.zh: 洵直復欲為大裘之裳，纁色而無章飾。

translations.literal: Xun Zhi furthermore wished to make a skirt for the great fur robe, vermilion in color and without patterned ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Zhi also proposed a vermilion, unpatterned skirt for the great fur robe.

sentences.zh: 夫裘安得有裳哉？

translations.literal: How could fur have a skirt?
translations.idiomatic: How could a fur robe have a skirt?

sentences.zh: 請從先帝所誌。

translations.literal: We ask to follow what the former emperor recorded.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to follow the former emperor's record.

sentences.zh: 其後詔如洵直議，去黑羔皮而以黑繒製焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter an edict followed Xun Zhi's proposal, removing black lamb fur and making it instead of black silk.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then adopted Xun Zhi's plan, replacing black lamb fur with black silk.

sentences.zh: 政和議禮局上：大裘，青表纁裏，黑羔皮為領、褾、襈，朱裳，被以袞服。

translations.literal: The Zhenghe Commission on Ritual submitted: the great fur robe, green outside and vermilion within, black lamb fur for collar, cuffs, and border, vermilion skirt, covered with the embroidered robe.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenghe ritual commission specified the great fur robe: green outside, vermilion lining, black lamb at collar, cuffs, and border, a vermilion skirt, and the embroidered robe as outer layer.

sentences.zh: 冬至祀昊天上帝服之，立冬祀黑帝、立冬後祭神州地祇亦如之。

translations.literal: It was worn at the winter solstice sacrifice to August Heaven, at the Start of Winter sacrifice to the Black Emperor, and likewise at the sacrifice to the Spirit of the Land after Start of Winter.
translations.idiomatic: It was worn at the winter solstice rite to August Heaven, at the Start of Winter rite to the Black Emperor, and at the land-spirit rite afterward.

sentences.zh: 中興之後，無有存者。

translations.literal: After the Restoration, none survived.
translations.idiomatic: After the Southern Song restoration, none remained.

sentences.zh: 紹興十三年，禮部侍郎王賞等言：“郊祀大禮，合依《禮經》，皇帝服大裘被袞行禮。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shaoxing, Vice Minister of Rites Wang Shang and others said: "For the great suburban sacrifice, one should follow the ritual classics: the emperor wears the great fur robe with the embroidered robe as outer layer to perform the rite."
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 13 (1143), Vice Minister Wang Shang and others argued: "The suburban sacrifice should follow the classics: the emperor should wear the great fur robe with the embroidered robe as cover.

sentences.zh: 據元豐詳定郊廟禮文，何洵直議以黑繒創作大裘如袞，惟領袖用黑羔。

translations.literal: According to the Yuanfeng detailed suburban and temple ritual texts, He Xunzhi proposed making the great fur robe of black silk in the form of the embroidered robe, using black lamb only for collar and sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanfeng suburban ritual code records He Xunzhi's proposal to shape the great fur robe like the embroidered robe in black silk, with black lamb only at collar and sleeves.

sentences.zh: 乞如洵直議。”

translations.literal: We beg to follow Xun Zhi's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to adopt Xun Zhi's plan."

sentences.zh: 詔有司如祖宗舊制，以羔製之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the officials to follow the ancestral old system and make it of lamb fur.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered officials to follow ancestral precedent and use lamb fur.

sentences.zh: 禮部又言：“關西羊羔，係天生黑色。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites again said: "Guanxi lambs are naturally black from birth.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites added: "Guanxi lambs are naturally black.

sentences.zh: 今有司涅白羔為之，不中禮製，不如權以繒代。

translations.literal: Now the officials dye white lambs to make it, which does not match ritual specification; it would be better temporarily to substitute silk."
translations.idiomatic: Officials now dyed white lambs black, which did not match the rite; they recommended temporarily using silk instead.

sentences.zh: 又元祐中，有司欲為大裘，度用百羔。

translations.literal: Also, in the Yuanyou era, when officials wished to make the great fur robe, they estimated using a hundred lambs.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou (1086–1094), officials planning the great fur robe estimated a hundred lambs would be needed.

sentences.zh: 哲宗以為害物，遂用黑繒。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong thought this harmed living things, and so black silk was used.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong objected on grounds of harm to animals, and black silk was used instead.

sentences.zh: 請依太常所言。”

translations.literal: We ask to follow what the Court of Imperial Sacrifices said.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to follow the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' recommendation."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂以袞襲裘，冕亦十二旒焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the embroidered robe was the outer layer over fur, and the coronet also had twelve pendants.
translations.idiomatic: The embroidered robe covered the fur, and the coronet bore twelve pendants.

sentences.zh: 袞冕之製。

translations.literal: The design of the embroidered robe and coronet.
translations.idiomatic: The embroidered robe and coronet.

sentences.zh: 宋初因五代之舊，天子之服有袞冕，廣一尺二寸，長二尺四寸，前後十二旒，二纊，並貫真珠。

translations.literal: Early in the Song, following Five Dynasties precedent, the Son of Heaven's dress included the embroidered robe and coronet, one foot two inches wide and two feet four inches long, twelve pendants front and back, two tassels, all strung with pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Early Song followed Five Dynasties usage: the emperor's embroidered robe and coronet was one foot two inches wide and two feet four long, with twelve pendants front and back, two tassels, all strung with pearls.

sentences.zh: 又有翠旒十二，碧鳳禦之，在珠旒外。

translations.literal: There were also twelve green jade pendants, controlled by green phoenixes, outside the pearl pendants.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve green jade pendants hung outside the pearl strands, borne on green phoenix mounts.

sentences.zh: 冕版以龍鱗錦表，上綴玉為七星，旁施琥珀瓶、犀瓶各二十四，周綴金絲網，鈿以真珠、雜寶玉，加紫雲白鶴錦裏。

translations.literal: The coronet board was faced with dragon-scale brocade, inlaid above with jade forming the Seven Stars, with twenty-four amber bottles and twenty-four rhinoceros-horn bottles at the sides, ringed with a gold-wire net, studded with pearls and assorted gems, with purple-cloud and white-crane brocade lining.
translations.idiomatic: The coronet board was faced with dragon-scale brocade, inlaid with jade in the pattern of the Seven Stars, flanked by twenty-four amber and twenty-four rhinoceros-horn bottle ornaments, ringed with a gold-wire net and studded with pearls and gems, lined with purple-cloud and white-crane brocade.

sentences.zh: 四柱飾以七寶，紅綾裏。

translations.literal: The four pillars were ornamented with the seven treasures, lined with red gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Four pillars were set with the seven treasures and lined in red gauze.

sentences.zh: 金飾玉簪導，紅絲絛組帶。

translations.literal: Gold ornaments, jade hairpin and chin strap, red silk cord and ribbon belt.
translations.idiomatic: It had gold fittings, a jade hairpin and chin strap, and a red silk cord belt.

sentences.zh: 亦謂之平天冠。

translations.literal: It was also called the Level Heaven Cap.
translations.idiomatic: It was also called the level-heaven cap.

sentences.zh: 袞服青色，日、月、星、山、龍、雉、虎蜼七章。

translations.literal: The embroidered robe was green, with seven emblems: sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragon, pheasant, and tiger-mountain pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The embroidered robe was green with seven emblems: sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragon, pheasant, and tiger-mountain motif.

sentences.zh: 紅裙，藻、火、粉米、黼、黻五章。

translations.literal: A red skirt bore five emblems: algae, fire, grain, axe-head, and opposing triangles.
translations.idiomatic: The red skirt bore five emblems: algae, fire, grain, axe-head, and opposing chevrons.

sentences.zh: 紅蔽膝，升龍二並織成，間以雲朵，飾以金鈒花鈿窠，裝以真珠、琥珀、雜寶玉。

translations.literal: A red knee cover with two ascending dragons woven together, interspersed with cloud patterns, ornamented with gold chased floral stud settings, decorated with pearls, amber, and assorted gems.
translations.idiomatic: The red knee cover had two woven ascending dragons among cloud motifs, with gold floral studs set with pearls, amber, and assorted gems.

sentences.zh: 紅羅襦裙，繡五章，青褾、襈、裾。

translations.literal: A red gauze jacket-skirt embroidered with five emblems, with green collar, cuffs, and hem.
translations.idiomatic: The red gauze jacket-skirt bore five embroidered emblems, with green collar, cuffs, and hem trim.

sentences.zh: 六采綬一，小綬三，結玉環三。

translations.literal: One six-colored sash, three small sashes, three jade ring knots.
translations.idiomatic: It included one six-colored sash, three smaller sashes, and three jade ring knots.

sentences.zh: 素大帶朱裏，青羅四神帶二，繡四神盤結。

translations.literal: A plain great belt with vermilion lining, two green gauze Four-Spirit belts, embroidered with coiled Four Spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The plain great belt had a vermilion lining; two green Four-Spirit belts were embroidered with coiled spirit motifs.

sentences.zh: 〈（綬帶飾並同袞服。）〉

translations.literal: (Sash and belt ornaments are the same as for the embroidered robe.)
translations.idiomatic: Sash and belt ornaments match those of the embroidered robe.]

sentences.zh: 白羅中單，青羅抹帶，紅羅勒帛。

translations.literal: White gauze inner robe, green gauze waist wrap, red gauze sash.
translations.idiomatic: Underneath were a white gauze inner robe, green waist wrap tie, and red sash.

sentences.zh: 鹿盧玉具劍，玉鏢首，鏤白玉雙佩，金飾貫真珠。

translations.literal: Deer-pattern jade-mounted sword, jade pommel, carved white jade double pendants, gold fittings strung with pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Accessories included a deer-pattern sword with jade fittings, jade pommel, carved white jade double pendants on pearl-strung gold mounts.

sentences.zh: 金龍鳳革帶，紅襪赤舄，金鈒花，四神玉鼻。

translations.literal: Gold dragon-phoenix leather belt, red socks and red shoes, gold chased floral ornament, Four-Spirit jade nose-piece.
translations.idiomatic: The set also had a gold dragon-phoenix leather belt, red socks and red shoes with gold floral chasing, and Four-Spirit jade shoe ornaments.

sentences.zh: 祭天地宗廟，朝太清宮、饗玉清昭應宮景靈宮、受冊尊號、元日受朝、冊皇太子則服之。

translations.literal: It was worn for sacrificing to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple; attending court at the Taiqing Palace; feasting at the Yuching, Zhaoying, and Jingling Palaces; receiving an honorific title; New Year's Day court audience; and investing the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: It was worn for sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestors; audiences at Taiqing Palace; banquets at Yuching, Zhaoying, and Jingling Palaces; investiture with honorific titles; New Year's court; and crowning the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 太祖建隆元年，太常禮院言：“準少府監牒，請具袞龍衣、絳紗袍、通天冠制度令式。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianlong under Emperor Taizu, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual Board said: "Per the petition from the Directorate of Palace Manufactories, please provide specifications for the embroidered dragon robe, deep-red gauze robe, and heaven-penetrating cap."
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 1 (960), the ritual board reported: "A petition from the Palace Manufactories requested formal specifications for the embroidered dragon robe, deep-red gauze robe, and heaven-penetrating cap.

sentences.zh: 袞冕，垂白珠十有二旒，以組為纓，色如其綬，黈纊充耳，玉簪導。

translations.literal: The embroidered robe and coronet: twelve hanging white pearl pendants, cord for the chin strap colored like the sash, yellow-black tassels as ear covers, jade hairpin and chin strap.
translations.idiomatic: The embroidered robe and coronet had twelve white pearl pendants, a cord chin strap matching the sash color, yellow-black ear tassels, and a jade hairpin with chin strap.

sentences.zh: 玄衣纁裳，十二章：八章在衣，日、月、星辰、山、龍、華蟲、火、宗彝；

translations.literal: Dark upper garment and vermilion skirt, twelve emblems: eight on the robe—sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragon, patterned creature, fire, and ancestral vessel;
translations.idiomatic: The dark upper robe and vermilion skirt bore twelve emblems—eight on the robe: sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragon, patterned creature, fire, and ancestral vessel;

sentences.zh: 四章在裳，藻、粉米、黼、黻。

translations.literal: Four on the skirt—algae, grain, axe-head, and opposing triangles.
translations.idiomatic: Four on the skirt: algae, grain, axe-head, and opposing chevrons.

sentences.zh: 衣褾領如上，為升龍，皆織就為之。

translations.literal: The robe's border and collar as above were ascending dragons, all woven finished.
translations.idiomatic: Collar and borders followed the same pattern of woven ascending dragons.

sentences.zh: 山、龍以下，每章一行，重以為等，每行十二。

translations.literal: From mountains and dragon downward, each emblem formed one row, graded by repetition, twelve per row.
translations.idiomatic: From the mountain and dragon motifs downward, each emblem occupied one row, repeated in ranks of twelve per row.

sentences.zh: 白紗中單，黼領，青褾、襈、裾。

translations.literal: White gauze inner robe, axe-head collar, green border, cuffs, and hem.
translations.idiomatic: The white gauze inner robe had an axe-head collar and green borders, cuffs, and hem.

sentences.zh: 蔽膝加龍、山、火三章。

translations.literal: The knee cover added three emblems: dragon, mountain, and fire.
translations.idiomatic: The knee cover added dragon, mountain, and fire emblems.

sentences.zh: 革帶，玉鉤䚢。

translations.literal: Leather belt, jade hook and pendant.
translations.idiomatic: Leather belt with jade hook and pendant.

sentences.zh: 大帶，素帶朱裏，紕其外，上朱下綠，紐約用組。

translations.literal: Great belt: plain belt with vermilion lining, red edge on the outside, vermilion above and green below, buttons and ties of cord.
translations.idiomatic: The great belt was plain with vermilion lining, red edging outside, vermilion above and green below, with cord buttons and ties.

sentences.zh: 鹿盧玉具劍，大珠鏢首，白玉雙佩，玄組。

translations.literal: Deer-pattern jade-mounted sword, large pearl pommel, white jade double pendants, dark cord.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a deer-pattern sword with jade fittings, large pearl pommel, white jade double pendants, and dark cord.

sentences.zh: 雙大綬六采，玄、黃、赤、白、縹、綠，純玄質，長二丈四尺五寸，首廣一尺。

translations.literal: Paired great six-colored sashes—dark, yellow, red, white, light blue, and green—with dark border, two zhang four chi five cun long, one chi wide at the head.
translations.idiomatic: Paired great six-colored sashes in dark, yellow, red, white, light blue, and green, with dark borders, measured two zhang four chi five cun long and one chi wide at the head.

sentences.zh: 小雙綬長二尺六寸，色同大綬，而首半之，間施三玉環。

translations.literal: Small paired sashes two chi six cun long, same colors as the great sash but half the width at the head, with three jade rings set between.
translations.idiomatic: Smaller paired sashes were two chi six cun long, matching the great sash colors at half the head width, with three jade rings between.

sentences.zh: 朱襪赤舄，加金飾。”

translations.literal: Vermilion socks and red shoes, with added gold ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion socks and red shoes with gold ornamentation."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 二年，太子詹事尹拙、工部尚書竇儀議：“謹按《周禮》：‘弁師掌王之五冕，朱裏延紐，五采繅，十有二就，皆五采玉十有二，玉笄朱紘。

translations.literal: In the second year, Supervisor of the Heir Apparent Yin Zhuo and Minister of Works Dou Yi submitted: "We respectfully cite the Rites of Zhou: 'The Cap Master handles the king's five coronets: vermilion lining, extended front cord, five-colored strings, twelve tassels, each with twelve five-colored jade beads, jade pin and vermilion chin cord.'"
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Yin Zhuo and Dou Yi argued: "We respectfully cite the Rites of Zhou: 'The Cap Master oversees the king's five coronets with vermilion lining, extended front cord, five-colored strings, twelve tassel rows of five-colored jade, jade pin, and vermilion chin cord.

sentences.zh: 諸侯之繅旒九就，瑉玉三采，其餘如王之事，繅斿皆就，玉瑱、玉笄。

translations.literal: For feudal lords the strings and pendants are nine tassels, min jade in three colors; the rest as for the king's duties—all strings and pendants as tassels, jade ear stoppers and jade pin.'
translations.idiomatic: Feudal lords had nine tassel rows with three-colored min jade; otherwise as for the king—all pendants as tassels, with jade ear stoppers and jade pin.

sentences.zh: ’疏云：‘王不言玉瑱，於此言之者，王與諸侯互相見為義。

translations.literal: The commentary says: 'The king's passage does not mention jade ear stoppers; it mentions them here so that king and feudal lords illuminate each other by contrast.'
translations.idiomatic: The commentary explains that the king's text omits jade ear stoppers but names them here so king and lords define each other by contrast.

sentences.zh: 是以王言玄冕、朱裏延紐及朱紘，明諸侯亦有之。

translations.literal: Therefore when the king mentions the dark coronet, vermilion lining, extended front cord, and vermilion chin cord, this shows feudal lords also have them.
translations.idiomatic: When the king's text lists the dark coronet, vermilion lining, extended front cord, and vermilion chin cord, it implies lords have them too.

sentences.zh: 諸公言玉瑱，明王亦有之。

translations.literal: When the lords' text mentions jade ear stoppers, this shows the king also has them.
translations.idiomatic: When the lords' text names jade ear stoppers, it shows the king has them as well.

sentences.zh: ’詳此經、疏之文，則是本有充耳。

translations.literal: Examining these passages of classic and commentary in detail, there originally were ear covers.
translations.idiomatic: Read together, classic and commentary show ear covers were originally prescribed.

sentences.zh: 今請令君臣袞冕以下並畫充耳，以合正文。”

translations.literal: We now ask that for emperor and ministers, from the embroidered robe and coronet downward, ear covers all be depicted, to accord with the canonical text.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that embroidered coronets for emperor and officials all depict ear covers, matching the canonical text."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年閏十二月，少府監楊格、少監王處訥等上新造皇帝冠冕。

translations.literal: In the intercalary twelfth month of the first year of Qiande, Director of Palace Manufactories Yang Ge, Vice Director Wang Chune, and others presented newly made imperial coronets.
translations.idiomatic: In intercalary twelfth month, Qiande 1 (964), Director Yang Ge, Vice Director Wang Chune, and others presented newly made imperial coronets.

sentences.zh: 先是，郊祀冠冕，多飾以珠玉，帝以華而且重，故命改製之。

translations.literal: Previously, suburban sacrifice coronets were heavily ornamented with pearls and jade; the emperor found them ornate and heavy, and therefore ordered them remade.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban coronets had been heavily jeweled; finding them ornate and heavy, the emperor ordered a redesign.

sentences.zh: 仁宗景祐二年，又以帝後及群臣冠服，多沿唐舊而循用之，久則有司浸為繁文，以失法度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyou under Emperor Renzong, because the empresses and court officials' caps and robes mostly followed Tang precedent and were continued in use, over time the officials gradually added elaborate ornament and lost proper standards.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyou 2 (1035), imperial consorts and officials still followed Tang cap-and-robe styles; over time officials had added ornate details and drifted from proper form.

sentences.zh: 詔入內內侍省、禦藥院與太常禮院詳典故，造冠冕，蠲減珍華，務從簡約，俾圖以進。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Inner Palace Domestic Service, Imperial Pharmacy, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual Board to examine classical precedents, make coronets, reduce precious ornament, strive for simplicity, and submit diagrams.
translations.idiomatic: An edict charged the inner domestic service, imperial pharmacy, and ritual board to research precedents, simplify coronets by stripping excess ornament, and submit designs.

sentences.zh: 續詔通天冠、絳紗袍更不修製。

translations.literal: A further edict stated that the heaven-penetrating cap and deep-red gauze robe would not be remade.
translations.idiomatic: A later edict exempted the heaven-penetrating cap and deep-red gauze robe from revision.

sentences.zh: 由是改製袞冕。

translations.literal: Thereupon the embroidered robe and coronet were remade.
translations.idiomatic: Only the embroidered robe and coronet were redesigned.

sentences.zh: 天版元闊一尺二寸，長二尺四寸，今製廣八寸，長一尺六寸。

translations.literal: The heaven board was originally one foot two inches wide and two feet four inches long; the new design is eight inches wide and one foot six inches long.
translations.idiomatic: The crown board, formerly one foot two inches by two feet four, was reduced to eight by sixteen inches.

sentences.zh: 減翠旒並鳳子，前後二十四珠旒並合典制。

translations.literal: The green jade pendants and phoenix mounts were removed; twenty-four pearl pendants front and back together match canonical regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Green jade pendants and phoenix mounts were dropped; twenty-four pearl pendants front and back now matched canonical rules.

sentences.zh: 天板頂上，元織成龍鱗錦為表，紫雲白鶴錦為裏，今製青羅為表，采畫出龍鱗，紅羅為裏，采畫出紫雲白鶴。

translations.literal: At the top of the heaven board, originally dragon-scale brocade was the face and purple-cloud white-crane brocade the lining; the new design uses green gauze as face with painted dragon scales, red gauze as lining with painted purple clouds and white cranes.
translations.idiomatic: The crown top, once dragon-scale brocade outside and purple-cloud white-crane brocade within, became green gauze painted with dragon scales outside and red gauze painted with clouds and cranes within.

sentences.zh: 所有犀瓶、琥珀瓶各二十四，今減不用。

translations.literal: The rhinoceros-horn bottles and amber bottles, twenty-four each, were now reduced and not used.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four rhinoceros and amber bottle ornaments on each side were eliminated.

sentences.zh: 金絲結網子上，舊有金絲結龍八，今減四，亦減絲令細。

translations.literal: On the gold-wire knotted net cap, there were originally eight gold-wire knotted dragons; now four were removed, and the wire was also made finer.
translations.idiomatic: The gold-wire net cap lost four of its eight wire dragons, and the wire was made finer.

sentences.zh: 天板四面花墜子、素墜子依舊，減輕造。

translations.literal: The floral and plain pendants on the four sides of the heaven board remained as before, but made lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Floral and plain side pendants on the crown board remained but were lightened.

sentences.zh: 冠身並天柱，元織成龍鱗錦，今用青羅，采畫出龍鱗；

translations.literal: The coronet body and heaven pillars were originally dragon-scale brocade; now green gauze is used, with painted dragon scales;
translations.idiomatic: The crown body and pillars, once dragon-scale brocade, became green gauze painted with dragon scales;

sentences.zh: 金輪等七寶，元真玉碾成，今更不用，如補空卻，以雲龍細窠。

translations.literal: The gold wheel and other seven treasures, originally cut from true jade, are no longer used; where spaces need filling, cloud-dragon fine pattern is used instead.
translations.idiomatic: The gold wheel and other seven-jewel ornaments, once carved jade, were replaced with fine cloud-dragon filler patterns.

sentences.zh: 分旒玉鉤二，今減去之。

translations.literal: Two jade hooks dividing the pendants were now removed.
translations.idiomatic: Two pendant-dividing jade hooks were removed.

sentences.zh: 天河帶、組帶、款慢帶依舊，減輕造。

translations.literal: The Milky Way belt, cord belt, and ceremonial sash remain as before, made lighter.
translations.idiomatic: The Milky Way belt, cord belt, and formal sash were kept but lightened.

sentences.zh: 納言，元用玉製，今用青羅，采畫出龍鱗錦。

translations.literal: The front speech-piece was originally of jade; now green gauze is used, painted to resemble dragon-scale brocade.
translations.idiomatic: The front ornament, once jade, became green gauze painted like dragon-scale brocade.

sentences.zh: 金棱上棱道，依舊用金，即減輕製。

translations.literal: The gold ridge and upper ridge channels still use gold, but are made lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Gold ridges and channels were retained but reduced in weight.

sentences.zh: 黈纊，玉簪。

translations.literal: Yellow-black ear tassels, jade hairpin.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow-black ear tassels and a jade hairpin.

sentences.zh: 袞服八章，日、月、星辰、山、龍、華蟲、火、宗彝，青羅身，紅羅襈，繡造。

translations.literal: The embroidered robe has eight emblems—sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragon, patterned creature, fire, and ancestral vessel—green gauze body, red gauze border, embroidered.
translations.idiomatic: The embroidered robe bore eight emblems—sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragon, patterned creature, fire, and ancestral vessel—on green gauze with red borders, all embroidered.

sentences.zh: 所有雲子，相度稀稠補空，更不用細窠，亦不使真珠裝綴。

translations.literal: All cloud-roundels are spaced according to density to fill gaps; fine patterns are no longer used, nor are pearls used for mounting.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud roundels were spaced to fill gaps; fine patterns and pearl mounts were dropped.

sentences.zh: 中單，依舊皂白製造。

translations.literal: The inner robe is still made black-and-white as before.
translations.idiomatic: The inner robe remained standard black-and-white.

sentences.zh: 裙用紅羅，繡出藻、粉米、黼、黻，周回花樣仍舊，減稀製之。

translations.literal: The skirt uses red gauze, embroidered with algae, grain, axe-head, and opposing triangles; the border floral pattern remains as before, made sparser.
translations.idiomatic: The red gauze skirt was embroidered with algae, grain, axe-head, and chevrons; border patterns were kept but thinned.

sentences.zh: 蔽膝用紅羅，繡升龍二，雲子補空，減稀製之，周回依舊，細窠不用。

translations.literal: The knee cover uses red gauze, embroidered with two ascending dragons, cloud-roundels filling gaps, made sparser; the border as before, fine patterns not used.
translations.idiomatic: The red knee cover had two ascending dragons and spaced cloud roundels; border design was kept but simplified, without fine patterns.

sentences.zh: 六采綬依舊，減絲織造。

translations.literal: The six-colored sash remains as before, woven with reduced silk.
translations.idiomatic: The six-colored sash was kept but woven with less silk.

sentences.zh: 所有玉環亦減輕。

translations.literal: All jade rings were also made lighter.
translations.idiomatic: The jade rings were lightened as well.

sentences.zh: 帶頭金葉減去，用銷金。

translations.literal: The gold leaf on the belt head was removed, and gilt instead was used.
translations.idiomatic: Gold leaf on the belt buckle was replaced with gilt work.

sentences.zh: 四神帶不用。

translations.literal: The four-spirit belt was not used.
translations.idiomatic: The four-spirit belt was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 劍、佩、梁、帶、襪、舄並依舊。

translations.literal: The sword, pendant, cap beams, belt, socks, and shoes all followed the old pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Sword, pendant, cap beams, belt, socks, and shoes were all left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐元年，王洙奏：“天子法服，冕旒形度重大，華飾稍繁，願集禮官參定。”

translations.literal: In the 1st year of Jiayou, Wang Zhu memorialized: "The emperor's ritual robes—the coronet pendants are large in form and weight, and the ornate trim is somewhat excessive; I ask that ritual officials be assembled to deliberate and fix them."
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou 1, Wang Zhu submitted that the emperor's court robes had coronet pendants too large and heavy and ornament too elaborate, and asked ritual officials to meet and settle the design.

sentences.zh: 詔禮院詳典禮上聞，而禮院繪圖以進。

translations.literal: [Closing memorial quote.] An edict ordered the Board of Ritual to examine the canonical rites and report upward, and the board submitted illustrated plans.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Board of Ritual to review canonical practice and report up; the board sent in drawings.

sentences.zh: 因敕禦藥院更造，其後，冕服稍增侈如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the Imperial Pharmacy to remake them; afterward the coronet robes again grew somewhat more lavish as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Pharmacy was then ordered to remake them, but afterward coronet dress again became somewhat more extravagant, as before.

sentences.zh: 英宗治平二年，知太常禮院李育奏曰：

translations.literal: In the 2nd year of Zhiping under Emperor Yingzong, Li Yu, director of the Board of Ritual in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: In Yingzong's Zhiping 2, Li Yu of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' Board of Ritual submitted:

sentences.zh: 郊廟之祭，本尚純質，袞冕之飾，皆存法象，非事繁侈、重奇玩也。

translations.literal: Sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temples originally prized pure simplicity; the adornments of the embroidered robe and coronet all preserve symbolic forms—they are not matters of profusion, luxury, or fondness for curios.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban and temple rites were meant to honor plain sincerity; embroidered robe and coronet ornaments embody ritual symbols, not extravagance or taste for rare objects.

sentences.zh: 冕則以《周官》為本，凡十二旒，間以采玉，加以紘、綖、笄、瑱之飾。

translations.literal: The coronet takes the Rites of Zhou as its basis: twelve pendants in all, interspersed with colored jade, plus adornments of the headband, forehead strap, hairpin, and ear-plug.
translations.idiomatic: The coronet followed the Rites of Zhou: twelve pendants set with colored jade, with headband, forehead strap, hairpin, and ear-plug ornaments.

sentences.zh: 袞則以《虞書》為始，凡十二章，首以辰象，別以衣裳繪繡之采。

translations.literal: The embroidered robe begins with the Canon of Yu: twelve emblems in all, headed by the celestial bodies, then separately rendered in the colors of painted and embroidered upper and lower garments.
translations.idiomatic: The embroidered robe began with the Canon of Yu: twelve emblems, led by sun, moon, and stars, then distinguished by the colors of painted and embroidered upper and lower dress.

sentences.zh: 東漢至唐，史官名儒，記述前製，皆無珠翠、犀寶之飾，何則？

translations.literal: From Eastern Han through Tang, court historians and eminent classicists recording earlier models mention no pearl, kingfisher-feather, or rhinoceros-horn adornments—why?
translations.idiomatic: From Eastern Han through Tang, historians and leading scholars describing earlier dress record no pearl, kingfisher, or rhinoceros-horn ornament—why?

sentences.zh: 鷸羽蜯胎，非法服所用；

translations.literal: Bittern feathers and mother-of-pearl are not suited for ritual robes;
translations.idiomatic: Kingfisher feathers and mother-of-pearl do not belong on ritual dress;

sentences.zh: 琥珀犀瓶，非至尊所冠；

translations.literal: amber and rhinoceros-horn bottles are not what the supreme sovereign should wear on his head;
translations.idiomatic: amber and rhinoceros-horn flasks are not fit for the Son of Heaven's crown;

sentences.zh: 龍錦七星，已列采章之內；

translations.literal: dragon brocade and the Seven Stars are already listed among the emblems of color;
translations.idiomatic: dragon brocade and the Seven Stars already appear among the prescribed emblems;

sentences.zh: 紫雲白鶴，近出道家之語，豈被袞戴璪、象天則數之義哉！

translations.literal: purple clouds and white cranes derive from recent Daoist language—how can these accord with wearing the embroidered robe and jade beads, symbolizing heaven and its numbered pattern!
translations.idiomatic: purple clouds and white cranes come from recent Daoist usage—how can they suit wearing the embroidered robe and beaded coronet that image heaven and its numbered order!

sentences.zh: 自大裘之廢，顓用袞冕，古樸稍去，而法度尚存。

translations.literal: Since the great fur robe fell into disuse and the embroidered robe and coronet alone were used, ancient simplicity was partly lost, yet canonical standards remained.
translations.idiomatic: Once the great fur robe was abandoned and only the embroidered robe and coronet were worn, some ancient plainness was lost, though ritual standards still survived.

sentences.zh: 夫明水大羹，不可以眾味和；

translations.literal: Clear water and plain broth cannot be seasoned with many flavors;
translations.idiomatic: Clear water and plain soup cannot be mixed with many flavors;

sentences.zh: 《雲門》《鹹池》，不可以新聲間；

translations.literal: "Cloud Gate" and "Salty Pond" cannot be interrupted by new music;
translations.idiomatic: "Cloud Gate" and "Salty Pond" cannot be interrupted by new tunes;

sentences.zh: 袞冕之服，不宜以珍怪累也。

translations.literal: Ritual dress of embroidered robe and coronet should not be burdened with rare and strange things.
translations.idiomatic: Embroidered robe and coronet should not be weighed down with exotic curios.

sentences.zh: 若魏明之用珊瑚，江左之用翡翠，侈靡衰播之餘，豈足為聖朝道哉！

translations.literal: If Emperor Ming of Wei used coral and the Jiangzuo regime used kingfisher feathers—remnants of extravagant decline—how can these serve as a model for our sage dynasty!
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Mingdi used coral and the Jiangzuo court used kingfisher feathers—survivals of decadent excess—what lesson could they offer our enlightened dynasty!

sentences.zh: 且太祖建隆元年少府監所造冕服，及二年博士聶崇義所進《三禮圖》，嚐詔尹拙、竇儀參校之，皆仿虞、周、漢、唐之舊。

translations.literal: Moreover, the coronet robes made by the Director of the Palace Revenues in the 1st year of Jianlong under Taizu, and the Illustrations of the Three Rites submitted in the 2nd year by Erudite Nie Chongyi, were once ordered reviewed by Yin Zhuo and Dou Yi—all modeled on the old systems of Yu, Zhou, Han, and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's first-year coronet robes from the Palace Revenues and Nie Chongyi's second-year Illustrations of the Three Rites had been sent to Yin Zhuo and Dou Yi for review—all patterned on Yu, Zhou, Han, and Tang precedent.

sentences.zh: 至四年冬服之，合祭天地於圜丘，用此製也。

translations.literal: By the 4th year they were worn in winter, when heaven and earth were jointly sacrificed at the Round Mound—this design was used.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth winter they were worn for the joint sacrifice to heaven and earth at the Round Mound—that was the form used.

sentences.zh: 太宗亦嚐命少府製於禁中，不聞改作。

translations.literal: Taizong also once ordered the Palace Revenues to make them within the palace; no alterations were heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong too had the Palace Revenues make them inside the palace, and no changes were recorded.

sentences.zh: 及真宗封泰山，禮官請服袞冕。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong enfeoffed Mount Tai, ritual officials requested he wear the embroidered robe and coronet.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong performed the Mount Tai feng sacrifice, ritual officers asked him to wear the embroidered robe and coronet.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“前王服羔裘，尚質也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Former kings wore lamb-fur robes, prizing simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Earlier kings wore lamb-fur robes and valued simplicity.

sentences.zh: 今則無羔裘而有袞冕，可從近製。”

translations.literal: Now there is no lamb-fur robe but there is the embroidered robe and coronet; one may follow the recent design."
translations.idiomatic: Today we have no lamb-fur robe but we do have the embroidered robe and coronet, so the recent design may be followed."

sentences.zh: 是豈有意於繁飾哉。

translations.literal: That was hardly an intent toward ornate trim.
translations.idiomatic: That was scarcely a wish for lavish ornament.

sentences.zh: 蓋後之有司，率意妄增，未嚐確議，遂相循而用。

translations.literal: Rather, later officials arbitrarily added at will, never having properly deliberated, and so the practice was handed down.
translations.idiomatic: Later offices simply added at whim without ever settling the matter, and the custom was passed on.

sentences.zh: 故仁宗嚐詔禮官章得象等詳議之，其所減過半，然不經之飾，重者多去，輕者尚存，不能盡如詔書之意。

translations.literal: Therefore Renzong once ordered ritual officials including Zhang Dexiang to deliberate in detail; more than half was cut—but among uncanonical adornments, the heavier were mostly removed while lighter ones remained, falling short of the edict's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong had Zhang Dexiang and other ritual officers review the dress in detail and cut more than half of the excess; the weightiest uncanonical ornaments were mostly removed, lighter ones remained, and the result still fell short of the edict.

sentences.zh: 故至和三年，王洙復議去繁飾，禮官畫圖以獻，漸還古禮，而有司所造，復如景祐之前。

translations.literal: Hence in the 3rd year of Zhihe, Wang Zhu again proposed removing ornate trim; ritual officials drew plans and submitted them, gradually restoring ancient rites—yet what officials made reverted to before Jingyou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhihe 3 Wang Zhu again urged stripping ornament; officers drew plans and moved back toward ancient rite, but what workshops produced again matched the pre-Jingyou style.

sentences.zh: 又按《開寶通禮》及《衣服令》，冕服皆有定法，悉無寶錦之飾。

translations.literal: Further examining the Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao and the Ordinance on Garments, coronet robes all have fixed regulations and entirely lack precious-brocade adornments.
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Rites of Kaibao and the Ordinance on Garments both fix coronet dress by rule and allow no precious-brocade ornament.

sentences.zh: 夫太祖、太宗富有四海，豈乏寶玩，顧不可施之郊廟也。

translations.literal: Taizu and Taizong possessed all within the four seas—were they short of treasures? Yet these could not be applied at suburban altars and temples.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu and Taizong ruled all under heaven and lacked no treasure, yet such things could not be worn at suburban altars and temples.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂，陛下肇祀天地，躬饗祖禰，服周之冕，觀古之象，願復先王之製，祖宗之法。

translations.literal: Your subject ventures to say: when Your Majesty begins sacrificing to heaven and earth and personally feasts the ancestral founders, wearing the Zhou coronet and contemplating ancient symbols, I pray you restore the designs of former kings and the law of our forefathers.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that when Your Majesty first sacrifices to heaven and earth and personally honors the ancestors in Zhou coronet, looking to ancient symbols, you should restore the former kings' dress and ancestral precedent.

sentences.zh: 其袞冕之服，及韠、綬、佩、舄之類，與《通禮》、《衣服令》、《三禮圖》制度不同者，宜悉改正。

translations.literal: As for the embroidered robe and coronet, knee aprons, sashes, pendants, shoes, and the like—where they differ from the Comprehensive Rites, Ordinance on Garments, and Illustrations of the Three Rites—they should all be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Embroidered robe and coronet, knee aprons, sashes, pendants, shoes, and the rest should all be brought into line wherever they diverge from the Comprehensive Rites, Ordinance on Garments, and Illustrations of the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 詔太常禮院、少府參定，遂合奏曰：

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Board of Ritual in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Palace Revenues to deliberate jointly; they memorialized together:
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices' Board of Ritual and the Palace Revenues were ordered to decide together and jointly submitted:

sentences.zh: 古者冕服之用，郊廟殊製。

translations.literal: In antiquity the use of coronet robes differed between suburban and temple rites.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times coronet dress differed for suburban altars and ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 唐興，天子之服有二等，而大裘尚存。

translations.literal: When Tang rose, the emperor's robes had two grades, and the great fur robe still remained.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang began, the emperor had two grades of dress, and the great fur robe still survived.

sentences.zh: 顯慶初，長孫無忌等采《郊特牲》之說，獻議廢大裘。

translations.literal: Early in the Xianqing era, Zhangsun Wuji and others, adopting the interpretation in "Special Regulations for Suburban Sacrifice," proposed abolishing the great fur robe.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xianqing, Zhangsun Wuji and others, following the "Special Regulations for Suburban Sacrifice," urged abolishing the great fur robe.

sentences.zh: 自是郊廟之祭，一用袞冕，然旒章之數，止以十二為節，亦未聞有餘飾也。

translations.literal: From then on suburban and temple sacrifices used only the embroidered robe and coronet; yet the number of pendant emblems was fixed at twelve, and no surplus adornments were heard of either.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter suburban and temple rites used only the embroidered robe and coronet; pendant emblems were limited to twelve, and no extra ornament was recorded.

sentences.zh: 國朝冕服，雖仿古製，然增以珍異巧縟，前世所未嚐有。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's coronet robes, though modeled on antiquity, added rare and ingeniously elaborate things never before seen.
translations.idiomatic: Our court's coronet dress, though based on antiquity, added rare and intricate ornament unknown to earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 夫國之大事，莫大於祀，而祭服違經，非以肅祀容、尊神明也。

translations.literal: Of the state's great affairs, none exceeds sacrifice—yet when sacrificial robes depart from the classics, that is not to solemnify the rite or honor the divine.
translations.idiomatic: No state matter surpasses sacrifice; sacrificial dress that departs from the classics neither dignifies the rite nor honors the spirits.

sentences.zh: 臣等以謂宜如育言，參酌《通禮》、《衣服令》、《三禮圖》及景祐三年減定之製，一切改造之。
