translations.literal: We hold it proper, as Li Yu said, to consult the Comprehensive Rites, Ordinance on Garments, Illustrations of the Three Rites, and the reductions fixed in the 3rd year of Jingyou, and remake everything.
translations.idiomatic: We hold, with Li Yu, that everything should be remade by the Comprehensive Rites, Ordinance on Garments, Illustrations of the Three Rites, and the Jingyou 3 reductions.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：“麻冕，禮也，今也純儉，吾從眾。”

translations.literal: Confucius said: "A hemp coronet is ritually correct, but today pure silk is economical—I follow the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "Hemp coronets are canonical, but now plain silk is simpler—I follow the common practice."

sentences.zh: 純者，絲也，變麻用絲，蓋已久矣。

translations.literal: Pure" means silk; replacing hemp with silk has been so for long.
translations.idiomatic: Pure means silk; the shift from hemp to silk had long since taken place.

sentences.zh: 則冕服之製，宜依舊以羅為之。

translations.literal: Thus the coronet robe should, as before, be made of gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Coronet dress should therefore continue to be made of gauze, as before.

sentences.zh: 冕廣一尺二寸，長二尺二寸，約以景表尺，前圓後方，黝上朱下，以金飾版側，以白玉珠為旒，貫之以五采絲繩。

translations.literal: The coronet is one foot two inches wide, two feet two inches long, roughly by the gnomon scale; round in front, square behind; black above, vermilion below; the board's sides gilt; white jade beads for pendants, strung on five-colored silk cord.
translations.idiomatic: The coronet was one foot two inches wide and two feet two inches long by the gnomon measure, round in front and square behind, black above and vermilion below, with gilt board edges and white jade pendants on five-colored silk.

sentences.zh: 前後各十二旒，旒各十二珠，相去一寸，長二尺。

translations.literal: Twelve pendants front and rear; each pendant twelve beads, one inch apart, two feet long.
translations.idiomatic: Front and rear each had twelve pendants of twelve beads, one inch apart and two feet long.

sentences.zh: 朱絲組為纓，黈纊充耳，金飾玉簪導。

translations.literal: Vermilion silk cord forms the chin strap; yellow-black floss fills the ears; jade hairpin with gold mount as guide.
translations.idiomatic: The chin strap was vermilion silk cord, the ear fillers yellow-black floss, and the guide a gold-mounted jade hairpin.

sentences.zh: 青衣纁裳，十二章：八章繪之於衣，日、月、星辰、山、龍、華蟲、火、宗彝也；

translations.literal: Azure upper garment, vermilion skirt—twelve emblems: eight painted on the robe—sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragon, patterned creature, fire, and ancestral vessel;
translations.idiomatic: The azure robe and vermilion skirt bore twelve emblems: eight painted on the upper garment—sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragon, patterned creature, fire, and ancestral vessel;

sentences.zh: 四章繡之於裳，藻、粉米、黼、黻也。

translations.literal: four embroidered on the skirt—algae, grain, axe-head, and opposing triangles.
translations.idiomatic: four embroidered on the skirt—algae, grain, axe-head, and chevrons.

sentences.zh: 錦龍褾、領，織為升龍。

translations.literal: Brocade dragon cuffs and collar, woven as ascending dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Cuffs and collar were brocade dragons woven as ascending dragons.

sentences.zh: 山、龍而下，一章為一行，重以為等，行十二。

translations.literal: From mountains and dragon downward, one emblem per row, repeated by rank—twelve rows.
translations.idiomatic: From mountains and dragon downward, one emblem per row, tiered by repetition—twelve rows.

sentences.zh: 別製大帶，素表朱裏，朱綠終辟。

translations.literal: A separate great belt: plain outer, vermilion inner, vermilion and green terminal borders.
translations.idiomatic: A separate great belt had a plain face, vermilion lining, and vermilion-green end borders.

sentences.zh: 韠、紱、舄，大小綬，亦去珠玉、鈿窠、琥珀、玻璃之飾。

translations.literal: Knee apron, ribbon, shoes, large and small sashes—also stripped of pearl, jade, filigree roundels, amber, and glass adornments.
translations.idiomatic: Knee aprons, ribbons, shoes, and large and small sashes likewise shed pearl, jade, filigree roundels, amber, and glass ornament.

sentences.zh: 其中單、革帶、玉具劍、玉佩、朱襪之製，已中禮令，無復改為，則法服有稽，祭禮增重。

translations.literal: As for the inner robe, leather belt, jade-mounted sword, jade pendant, and vermilion socks—their forms already match ritual ordinances and need no further change; then ritual robes have a basis and sacrificial rites gain weight.
translations.idiomatic: The inner robe, leather belt, jade-mounted sword, jade pendant, and vermilion socks already matched ritual ordinance and needed no change; with that, court dress had a standard and sacrifice gained dignity.

sentences.zh: 復詔禮院再詳以聞。

translations.literal: An edict again ordered the Board of Ritual to examine further and report.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Ritual was again ordered to review the matter and report.

sentences.zh: 而內侍省奏謂：“景祐中已裁定，可因而用也。”

translations.literal: But the Directorate of Palace Attendants memorialized: "It was already fixed in Jingyou; that may be used as is."
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Palace Attendants replied: "This was already settled in Jingyou and may be used unchanged."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approval was granted.

sentences.zh: 神宗元豐元年，詳定郊廟禮文所言：

translations.literal: In the 1st year of Yuanfeng under Shenzong, the Detailed Regulations for Suburban and Temple Rites stated:
translations.idiomatic: In Shenzong's the first year of Yuanfeng, the Detailed Regulations for Suburban and Temple Rites reported:

sentences.zh: 凡冕版廣八寸，長尺六寸，與古製相合，更不復議。

translations.literal: Generally the coronet board is eight inches wide, one foot six inches long—matching antiquity; no further debate.
translations.idiomatic: The coronet board, eight inches wide and one foot six inches long, matched antiquity and needed no further discussion.

sentences.zh: 今取少府監進樣，如以青羅為表，紅羅為裏，則非《弁師》所謂“玄冕朱裏’者也。

translations.literal: Now taking the sample submitted by the Director of Palace Revenues: if green gauze is outer and red gauze inner, that is not what the "Master of Caps" calls "dark coronet with vermilion lining."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Revenues' sample used green gauze outside and red gauze inside, unlike the Master of Caps' "dark coronet with vermilion lining."

sentences.zh: 上用金棱天板，四周金絲結網，兩旁用真珠、花素墜之類，皆不應禮。

translations.literal: Above, a gilt heaven board; around the sides a gold-wire mesh; on both flanks pearls, floral plain pendants, and the like—all contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Its gilt heaven board, gold-wire mesh around the sides, and pearl and floral pendants on both flanks all violated ritual.

sentences.zh: 伏請改用朱組為紘，玉笄、玉瑱，以玄紞垂瑱，以五采玉貫於五色藻為旒，以青、赤、黃、白、黑五色備為一玉，每一玉長一寸，前後二十四旒，垂而齊肩，以合孔子所謂純儉之義。

translations.literal: We respectfully ask that vermilion cord replace the headband, jade hairpin and ear-plug, dark cord suspending the plug, five-colored jade strung on five-colored tassels as pendants—each jade combining green, red, yellow, white, and black, each one inch long; twenty-four pendants front and rear, hanging level with the shoulders, to accord with Confucius's meaning of pure economy.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that vermilion cord serve as headband, with jade hairpin and ear-plug, dark cord suspending the plug, and pendants of five-colored jade on five-colored tassels—each bead combining green, red, yellow, white, and black, one inch long; twenty-four pendants front and rear, hanging to the shoulders, in the plain economy Confucius praised.

sentences.zh: 又古者祭服、朝服之裳，皆前三幅，後四幅，前為陽以象奇，後為陰以象偶。

translations.literal: In antiquity the skirts of sacrificial and court robes had three panels in front and four behind—front as yang symbolizing odd numbers, rear as yin symbolizing even.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sacrificial and court skirts had three panels in front and four behind—front as yang for odd numbers, rear as yin for even.

sentences.zh: 惟深衣、中襌之屬連衣裳，而裳復不殊前後，然以六幅交解為十二幅，象十二月。

translations.literal: Only deep robes and inner garments join upper and lower; their skirts do not distinguish front and rear, yet six panels crossed make twelve, symbolizing the twelve months.
translations.idiomatic: Only deep robes and inner dress joined upper and lower without distinguishing front and rear skirts, yet six crossed panels made twelve, for the twelve months.

sentences.zh: 其製作莫不有法，故謂之法服。

translations.literal: In every detail of their making there is regulation—hence they are called ritual robes.
translations.idiomatic: Every part of their making followed rule—hence the name ritual dress.

sentences.zh: 今少府監袞服，其裳乃以八幅為之，不殊前後，有違古義。

translations.literal: Now the Palace Revenues' embroidered robe makes its skirt of eight panels, undifferentiated front and rear—contrary to ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Revenues' embroidered robe used an eight-panel skirt without front-rear distinction, contrary to ancient usage.

sentences.zh: 伏請改正祭服之裳，以七幅為之，殊其前後。

translations.literal: We respectfully ask that sacrificial skirts be corrected to seven panels, distinguishing front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that sacrificial skirts be corrected to seven panels with front and rear distinguished.

sentences.zh: 以今太常周尺度之，幅廣二尺二寸，每幅兩旁各縫殺一寸，謂之削幅，腰間辟積無數。

translations.literal: Measured by today's Zhou scale in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices: each panel two feet two inches wide; one inch trimmed from each side of every panel—called "shaved panels"; pleats at the waist without fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: By the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' Zhou measure, each panel was two feet two inches wide, with one inch trimmed from each side—"shaved panels"—and unfixed waist pleats.

sentences.zh: 裳側有純，謂之綼；

translations.literal: At the skirt's sides a border called the side hem;
translations.idiomatic: A border at the skirt's sides was called the side hem;

sentences.zh: 裳下有純，謂之钅易。

translations.literal: At the skirt's bottom a border called the lower hem.
translations.idiomatic: a border at the skirt's bottom was called the lower hem.

sentences.zh: 綼、緆之廣各寸半，表裏合為三寸。

translations.literal: Side and lower borders each one and a half inches wide; outer and inner together three inches.
translations.idiomatic: Side and lower borders were each one and a half inches wide, three inches together inside and out.

sentences.zh: 群臣祭服之裳，仿此。

translations.literal: Court ministers' sacrificial skirts should follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers' sacrificial skirts were to follow this pattern.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approval was granted.

sentences.zh: 政和議禮局更上皇帝冕服之製：冕版廣八寸，長一尺六寸，前高八寸五分，後高九寸五分。

translations.literal: The Ritual Deliberation Bureau in the Zhenghe era further submitted the emperor's coronet design: board eight inches wide, one foot six inches long; front height eight inches five fen, rear nine inches five fen.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe the Ritual Deliberation Bureau submitted the emperor's coronet: an eight-by-one-foot-six board, front height eight inches five fen, rear nine inches five fen.

sentences.zh: 青表朱裏，前後各十有二旒，五采藻十有二就，就間相去一寸。

translations.literal: Green outer, vermilion inner; twelve pendants front and rear; twelve five-colored tassel clusters, one inch between clusters.
translations.idiomatic: Green outside and vermilion inside; twelve pendants front and rear; twelve five-colored tassel clusters, one inch apart.

sentences.zh: 青碧錦織成天河帶，長一丈二尺，廣二寸。

translations.literal: Green-blue brocade woven as a Milky Way band, twelve feet long, two inches wide.
translations.idiomatic: A Milky Way band of green-blue brocade, twelve feet long and two inches wide.

sentences.zh: 朱絲組帶為纓，黈纊充耳，金飾玉簪導，長一尺二寸。

translations.literal: Vermilion silk cord as chin strap, yellow-black floss fills ears, gold-mounted jade hairpin guide, one foot two inches long.
translations.idiomatic: The chin strap was vermilion silk cord, ear fillers yellow-black floss, and the gold-mounted jade hairpin guide one foot two inches long.

sentences.zh: 袞服，青衣八章，繪日、月、星辰、山、龍、華蟲、火、宗彝；

translations.literal: Embroidered robe: azure robe eight emblems, painted sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragon, patterned creature, fire, and ancestral vessel;
translations.idiomatic: The embroidered robe had an azure upper garment with eight painted emblems—sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragon, patterned creature, fire, and ancestral vessel;

sentences.zh: 纁裳四章，繡藻、粉米、黼、黻。

translations.literal: vermilion skirt four emblems, embroidered algae, grain, axe-head, and chevrons.
translations.idiomatic: and a vermilion skirt with four embroidered emblems—algae, grain, axe-head, and chevrons.

sentences.zh: 蔽膝隨裳色，繡升龍二。

translations.literal: Knee cover matching skirt color, two ascending dragons embroidered.
translations.idiomatic: The knee cover matched the skirt and bore two embroidered ascending dragons.

sentences.zh: 白羅中單，皂褾、襈，紅羅勒帛，青羅襪帶。

translations.literal: White gauze inner robe, black cuffs and border, red gauze girdle, green gauze sock ties.
translations.idiomatic: There was a white gauze inner robe, black cuffs and border, red gauze girdle, and green gauze sock ties.

sentences.zh: 緋白羅大帶，革帶，白玉雙佩。

translations.literal: Crimson-white gauze great belt, leather belt, paired white jade pendants.
translations.idiomatic: A crimson-white gauze great belt, leather belt, and paired white jade pendants completed the set.

sentences.zh: 大綬六采，赤、黃、黑、白、縹、綠，小綬三色，如大綬，間施玉環三。

translations.literal: Great sash six colors—red, yellow, black, white, light blue, and green; small sash three colors like the great sash, with three jade rings interspersed.
translations.idiomatic: The great sash used six colors—red, yellow, black, white, light blue, and green; the small sash matched it in three colors with three jade rings set between.

sentences.zh: 朱襪，赤舄，緣以黃羅。

translations.literal: Vermilion socks, red shoes, bordered with yellow gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion socks and red shoes were edged with yellow gauze.

sentences.zh: 中興仍舊制，延，以羅衣木，玄表朱裏，長尺有六寸，前低一寸二分，四旁緣以金，覆於卷武之上，繅以五色絲貫五色玉，前後各十二，凡用二百八十有八。

translations.literal: After the Restoration the old system was kept. The brim was made of gauze, black outer and vermilion inner, one foot six inches long, one inch two fen lower in front; the four sides bordered with gold, covering the rolled crown base; five-colored silk strung with five-colored jade, twelve front and rear, two hundred eighty-eight in all.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynastic restoration the old form was kept: a gauze brim, black outside and vermilion inside, one foot six inches long and one inch two fen lower in front, gold-edged on four sides over the rolled crown base, with five-colored silk threading five-colored jade—twelve front and rear, two hundred eighty-eight in all.

sentences.zh: 玉笄，充耳用黃綿，紘以朱組，以其一屬於左笄上垂下，又屈而屬於右笄，係之而垂其餘。

translations.literal: Jade hairpin; yellow floss filled the ears; vermilion cord as headband, one end attached to the left hairpin hanging down, then bent to attach to the right hairpin, tied and the rest left hanging.
translations.idiomatic: A jade hairpin; yellow floss filled the ears; vermilion cord as headband ran from the left hairpin down, bent to the right hairpin, tied, and hung free.

sentences.zh: 玄衣，八章，升龍於山，繪。

translations.literal: Black upper garment, eight emblems; ascending dragon on mountains, painted.
translations.idiomatic: The black upper garment bore eight emblems, with ascending dragon on mountains painted.

sentences.zh: 裳纁，四章，繡。

translations.literal: Vermilion skirt, four emblems, embroidered.
translations.idiomatic: The vermilion skirt had four embroidered emblems.

sentences.zh: 幅前三後四，斷而不屬，兩旁殺縫，腰辟積，綼緆之廣皆如舊。

translations.literal: Three panels in front and four behind, cut separately and not joined; side seams trimmed; waist pleats; side and lower border widths all as before.
translations.idiomatic: Three front panels and four rear, cut apart rather than joined, with trimmed side seams and waist pleats; side and lower border widths remained as before.

sentences.zh: 大帶以緋白羅合而紩之，以朱綠飾其側，上朱下綠，其束處以組為紐約，下垂三尺。

translations.literal: The great belt joined crimson and white gauze and stitched them; vermilion and green bordered the sides, vermilion above and green below; at the binding point a cord knot, hanging three feet down.
translations.idiomatic: The great belt joined crimson and white gauze; vermilion and green edged the sides, vermilion above and green below, with a cord knot at the bind and a three-foot drop.

sentences.zh: 通天冠、絳紗袍亦如之。

translations.literal: The heaven-penetrating cap and deep-red gauze robe were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The heaven-penetrating cap and deep-red gauze robe followed the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 白羅中單，領、褾、襈以黻，服裘則以皂。

translations.literal: White gauze inner robe; collar, cuffs, and border with chevrons; when wearing fur, black.
translations.idiomatic: The white gauze inner robe had collar, cuffs, and border in chevrons; when wearing fur dress, black.

sentences.zh: 絳紗袍則衣用白紗，領、褾、襈以朱。

translations.literal: For the deep-red gauze robe the garment used white gauze, collar, cuffs, and border in vermilion.
translations.idiomatic: With the deep-red gauze robe the body was white gauze and collar, cuffs, and border vermilion.

sentences.zh: 綬大小各一，大綬織以六采，青、黃、黑、白、縹、綠，下垂青絲網，上有結，垂玉環三；

translations.literal: Large and small sashes one each; the great sash woven in six colors—green, yellow, black, white, light blue, and green—with a green silk net hanging below, a knot above, and three jade rings suspended;
translations.idiomatic: There was one great and one small sash; the great sash was woven in six colors—green, yellow, black, white, light blue, and green—with a green silk net below, a knot above, and three jade rings hanging;

sentences.zh: 小綬製如大綬，惟三色。

translations.literal: the small sash made like the great sash, but only three colors.
translations.idiomatic: the small sash matched the great sash in make but used only three colors.

sentences.zh: 大裘、絳紗袍皆用之。

translations.literal: Both the great fur robe and deep-red gauze robe used them.
translations.idiomatic: Both the great fur robe and deep-red gauze robe used these sashes.

sentences.zh: 革帶，博二寸，革為裏，緋羅為表，飾以玉銙，鈕以下鉤䚢。

translations.literal: Leather belt, two inches wide, leather lining, crimson gauze face, ornamented with jade plaques; below the buttons, hooks and corner pieces.
translations.idiomatic: The leather belt was two inches wide, leather-lined and crimson-gauze-faced, set with jade plaques and hooks and corner pieces below the buttons.

sentences.zh: 通天冠、絳紗袍亦用之。

translations.literal: The heaven-penetrating cap and deep-red gauze robe also used it.
translations.idiomatic: The heaven-penetrating cap and deep-red gauze robe used it as well.

sentences.zh: 韍從裳色，上有紕，下有純，去上五寸，繪以山、龍、火，上接革帶係之。

translations.literal: The knee apron matched the skirt color; an upper border above and lower border below, five inches from the top, painted with mountains, dragon, and fire, tied to the leather belt above.
translations.idiomatic: The knee apron matched the skirt, with upper and lower borders five inches from the top painted with mountains, dragon, and fire, and tied to the leather belt above.

sentences.zh: 佩有衡，有琚瑀，有衝牙，係於革帶，左右各一。

translations.literal: The pendant had a crossbar, square and semicircular pieces, and angled tooth, tied to the leather belt, one on each side.
translations.idiomatic: The pendant set had a crossbar, square and semicircular jades, and an angled tooth, fastened to the leather belt on left and right.

sentences.zh: 上設衡，衡下垂三帶，貫以蠙珠。

translations.literal: Above was set a crossbar; from the crossbar hung three strands, strung with pearl beads.
translations.idiomatic: At the top was a crossbar from which three strands hung, threaded with pearl beads.

sentences.zh: 次則中有金獸麵，兩旁夾以雙璜，又次設琚瑀。

translations.literal: Next within was a gold beast-face, flanked on both sides by paired semicircular jades; below that again were set the square and semicircular pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Below that, a gold beast-face sat at center, flanked by paired semicircular jades, with square and semicircular jades set beneath.

sentences.zh: 下則衝牙居中央，兩旁有玉滴子，行則擊牙而有聲。

translations.literal: Below, the angled tooth occupied the center; on both sides were jade drops; when walking, the tooth was struck and made sound.
translations.idiomatic: At the bottom the angled tooth sat in the center, with jade drops on either side; in motion the tooth struck and rang.

sentences.zh: 舄有絇，有純，有繶，有綦，以緋羅為之，首加金飾。

translations.literal: The shoes had laces, borders, embroidery, and ties, made of crimson gauze, with gold ornament added at the toe.
translations.idiomatic: The court shoes had laces, borders, embroidery, and ties of crimson gauze, with gold ornament at the toe.

sentences.zh: 服通天冠、絳紗袍則用黑舄，以烏皮為之。

translations.literal: When wearing the heaven-penetrating cap and deep-red gauze robe, black shoes were used, made of black leather.
translations.idiomatic: With the heaven-penetrating cap and deep-red gauze robe one wore black court shoes of black leather.

sentences.zh: 常服則用白舄，以絲為之。

translations.literal: For everyday dress, white shoes were used, made of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Everyday dress used white court shoes of silk.

sentences.zh: 襪，羅表繒裏，施靿著綦以係之，赤舄以朱，黑舄以白，白舄同。

translations.literal: Socks: gauze outer and silk inner, the top fitted with ties to fasten them; red shoes used vermilion, black shoes white, white shoes likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Socks were gauze outside and silk inside, with a fitted top and ties to hold them; red shoes paired with vermilion, black with white, and white shoes likewise.

sentences.zh: 通天冠。

translations.literal: The heaven-penetrating cap.
translations.idiomatic: The heaven-penetrating cap.

sentences.zh: 二十四梁，加金博山，附蟬十二，高廣各一尺。

translations.literal: Twenty-four ridges, with gold sacred-mountain ornament added, twelve cicada ornaments attached, height and width each one foot.
translations.idiomatic: It had twenty-four ridges, a gilded sacred-mountain finial, twelve cicada ornaments, and was one foot high and wide.

sentences.zh: 青表朱裏，首施珠翠，黑介幘，組纓翠緌，玉犀簪導。

translations.literal: Green outer and vermilion inner, pearls and kingfisher feathers set at the front, black inner cap, cord tassel with green tassel-tip, jade rhinoceros-horn hairpin and guide.
translations.idiomatic: Green outside and vermilion within, with pearls and kingfisher feathers at the front, a black inner cap, green tassel on the cord, and a jade rhinoceros horn hairpin as guide.

sentences.zh: 絳紗袍，以織成雲龍紅金條紗為之，紅裏，皂褾、襈、裾，絳紗裙，蔽膝如袍飾，並皂褾、襈。

translations.literal: Deep-red gauze robe, made of woven cloud-dragon red-and-gold striped gauze, red lining, black cuffs, border, and hem; deep-red gauze skirt; knee cover ornamented like the robe, also with black cuffs and border.
translations.idiomatic: The deep-red gauze robe was woven cloud-and-dragon gauze with red-gold stripes, red-lined with black cuffs, border, and hem; its deep-red gauze skirt and knee cover matched the robe, likewise with black cuffs and border.

sentences.zh: 白紗中單，朱領、褾、襈、裾。

translations.literal: White gauze inner robe, vermilion collar, cuffs, border, and hem.
translations.idiomatic: A white gauze inner robe with vermilion collar, cuffs, border, and hem.

sentences.zh: 白羅方心曲領。

translations.literal: White gauze square-heart curved collar.
translations.idiomatic: A white gauze square-heart curved collar.

sentences.zh: 白襪，黑舄，佩綬如袞。

translations.literal: White socks, black shoes, sash pendant like the embroidered robe.
translations.idiomatic: White socks and black shoes, with sash and pendant as for the embroidered robe.

sentences.zh: 大祭祀致齋、正旦冬至五月朔大朝會、大冊命、親耕籍田皆服之。

translations.literal: Great sacrifices with fasting, New Year's Day, winter solstice, first day of the fifth month grand court assemblies, grand investiture, and personal plowing of the sacred field—all wore it.
translations.idiomatic: It was worn for great sacrifices after fasting, New Year's Day and winter solstice, the first-of-May grand court, grand investiture, and the emperor's plowing of the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 仁宗天聖二年，南郊，禮儀使李維言：“通天冠上一字，準敕回避。”

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiansheng under Emperor Renzong, at the southern suburb sacrifice, the Commissioner of Ritual Protocol Li Wei said: "The taboo character in the name heaven-penetrating cap must be avoided, as the edict requires."
translations.idiomatic: In Tiansheng 2 (1024), at the southern suburb rite, Ritual Commissioner Li Wei said: "The taboo character in the name heaven-penetrating cap must be avoided, as the edict requires."

sentences.zh: 詔改承天冠。

translations.literal: An edict changed it to the heaven-receiving cap.
translations.idiomatic: An edict renamed it the heaven-receiving cap.

sentences.zh: 中興之製，冠高九寸，服用並同。

translations.literal: Under the Restoration design, the cap was nine inches high; dress and use were all the same.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynastic restoration the cap was nine inches high; the rest of the regalia was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 乾道九年，又用履袍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qiandao, the footed robe was again used.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 9 (1173) the footed robe was adopted again.

sentences.zh: 袍以絳羅為之，折上巾，通犀金玉帶。

translations.literal: The robe was made of deep-red gauze, folded-up cap, full rhinoceros-horn and jade-gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: The robe was deep-red gauze, worn with a folded-up cap and a belt of rhinoceros horn, jade, and gold.

sentences.zh: 係履，則曰履袍；

translations.literal: When tied with shoes, it was called the footed robe;
translations.idiomatic: With slippers it was called the footed robe;

sentences.zh: 服靴，則曰靴袍。

translations.literal: When wearing boots, it was called the booted robe.
translations.idiomatic: With boots it was called the booted robe.

sentences.zh: 履、靴皆用黑革。

translations.literal: Both shoes and boots used black leather.
translations.idiomatic: Slippers and boots were both black leather.

sentences.zh: 四孟朝獻景靈宮、郊祀、明堂，詣宮、宿廟、進胙，上壽兩宮及端門肆赦，並服之。

translations.literal: The four first-month offerings at Jingling Palace, suburban and Bright Hall sacrifices, visits to the palace, overnight at the temple, presenting sacrificial meat, birthday felicitations to both palaces, and amnesty at Duan Gate—all wore it.
translations.idiomatic: It was worn for the four first-month offerings at Jingling Palace, suburban and Bright Hall rites, palace visits, overnight temple stays, presenting sacrificial meat, birthday felicitations to both palaces, and amnesty proclamations at Duan Gate.

sentences.zh: 大禮畢還宮，乘平輦，服亦如之。

translations.literal: When the great rite was complete and the palace was re-entered, riding the level palanquin, dress was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: After a great rite, returning to the palace in the level palanquin, the same dress applied.

sentences.zh: 若大輦，則服通天、絳紗如常儀。

translations.literal: If the great palanquin, then wore heaven-penetrating cap and deep-red gauze as in regular protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In the great palanquin one wore the heaven-penetrating cap and deep-red gauze robe per usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 衫袍。

translations.literal: Robe-jacket.
translations.idiomatic: The robe-jacket.

sentences.zh: 唐因隋製，天子常服赤黃、淺黃袍衫，折上巾，九還帶，六合靴。

translations.literal: Tang followed Sui practice: for everyday dress the Son of Heaven wore red-yellow and light yellow robe-jackets, a folded-up cap, a nine-loop belt, and six-harmony boots.
translations.idiomatic: Tang followed Sui practice: the emperor's everyday dress was red-yellow and light yellow robe-jackets, a folded-up cap, a nine-loop belt, and six-harmony boots.

sentences.zh: 宋因之，有赭黃、淡黃袍衫，玉裝紅束帶，皂文鞸，大宴則服之。

translations.literal: Song followed this: there were ochre-yellow and pale yellow robe-jackets with jade-mounted red waist sashes and black patterned boots, worn at great banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Song followed suit: ochre-yellow and pale yellow robe-jackets with jade-mounted red waist sashes and black patterned boots were worn at great banquets.

sentences.zh: 又有赭黃、淡黃衤癸袍，紅衫袍，常朝則服之。

translations.literal: There were also ochre-yellow and pale yellow slit robes and red robe-jackets, worn at regular court.
translations.idiomatic: There were also ochre-yellow and pale yellow slit robes and red robe-jackets for regular court audiences.

sentences.zh: 又有窄袍，便坐視事則服之。

translations.literal: There was also the narrow robe, worn when conducting business seated informally.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the narrow robe, worn when holding court seated informally.

sentences.zh: 皆皂紗折上巾，通犀金玉環帶。

translations.literal: All used black gauze folded-up caps and belts with rhinoceros horn, jade, and gold rings.
translations.idiomatic: All were worn with black gauze folded-up caps and belts set with rhinoceros horn, jade, and gold rings.

sentences.zh: 窄袍或禦烏紗帽。

translations.literal: For the narrow robe one sometimes wore the black gauze cap.
translations.idiomatic: For the narrow robe the emperor sometimes wore the black gauze cap instead.

sentences.zh: 中興仍之。

translations.literal: After the Restoration the practice remained.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynastic restoration the practice remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 初，高宗踐祚於南都，隆祐太后命內臣上乘輿服禦，有小冠。

translations.literal: Initially, when Emperor Gaozong acceded at the Southern Capital, Empress Dowager Longyou had inner attendants present riding dress for the emperor, including a small crown.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong first acceded at the Southern Capital, Empress Dowager Longyou had inner attendants bring riding dress for the emperor, including a small crown.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：“祖宗閑居之所服也，自神宗始易以巾。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "This is what the ancestors wore at leisure; from Emperor Shenzong onward it was changed to the cap.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said: "This is what the ancestors wore at leisure; from Emperor Shenzong onward it was changed to the cap.

sentences.zh: 願即位後，退朝上戴此冠，庶幾如祖宗時氣象。”

translations.literal: After accession, when leaving court and returning to the palace, may Your Majesty wear this crown, so that the court may recover something of the ancestral atmosphere."
translations.idiomatic: After accession, when leaving court and returning to the palace, may Your Majesty wear this crown, so that the court may recover something of the ancestral atmosphere."

sentences.zh: 後殿早講，皇帝服帽子，紅袍，玉束帶，講讀官公服係鞋。

translations.literal: For the morning lecture in the rear hall, the emperor wore a cap, red robe, and jade waist sash, and the lecture and reading officers wore official dress with tied shoes.
translations.idiomatic: For the morning lecture in the rear hall, the emperor wore a cap, red robe, and jade waist sash, and the lecture and reading officers wore official dress with tied shoes.

sentences.zh: 晚講，皇帝服頭巾，背子，講官易便服。

translations.literal: For the evening lecture, the emperor wore a headcloth and sleeveless jacket, and the lecture officers changed into informal dress.
translations.idiomatic: For the evening lecture, the emperor wore a headcloth and sleeveless jacket, and the lecture officers changed into informal dress.

sentences.zh: 此嘉定四年講筵之製也。

translations.literal: This was the lecture-hall protocol established in the fourth year of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: This was the lecture-hall protocol established in Jiading 4 (1211).

sentences.zh: 禦閱服。

translations.literal: Review attire.
translations.idiomatic: Review attire.

sentences.zh: 以金裝甲，乘馬大閱則服之。

translations.literal: Gold-plated armor; worn when mounted for the great military review.
translations.idiomatic: Gold-plated armor worn for the great mounted review.

sentences.zh: 圭。

translations.literal: The jade tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The jade tablet.

sentences.zh: 宋初，凡大祭祀、大朝會，天子皆執圭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, for all great sacrifices and great court assemblies, the Son of Heaven all held the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty the emperor held a jade tablet at every great sacrifice and grand court assembly.

sentences.zh: 元豐二年，詳定儀注所言：“《周禮》：‘王執鎮圭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng, the Detailed Determination Office on ritual directives said: "The Rites of Zhou: 'The king holds the tablet of dominion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanfeng (1079) the ritual commission reported: "The Rites of Zhou says, 'The king holds the tablet of dominion.

sentences.zh: ’釋者曰：‘祭天地宗廟及朝日、夕月，則執之。

translations.literal: ' The commentator says: 'When sacrificing to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and at the sunrise and moonset rites, then one holds it.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator explains that it is held for sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temple, and at the sunrise and moonset rites.

sentences.zh: 若朝覲，諸侯授玉於王，王受玉，撫玉而已。

translations.literal: If at an audience, the feudal lords present jade to the king; the king receives the jade and merely strokes the jade.'
translations.idiomatic: At an audience the feudal lords present jade to the king, who receives it and only strokes the jade.'

sentences.zh: ’《考工記》：‘天子執冒四寸，以朝諸侯。

translations.literal: ' The Records of Craftsmen: 'The Son of Heaven holds the cover four inches, to hold audience with the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: The Records of Craftsmen says the Son of Heaven holds a four-inch cover-tablet when receiving the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: ’蓋天子以冒圭邪刻之處，冒諸侯之圭，以齊瑞信也。

translations.literal: ' For the Son of Heaven, using the beveled notch of the cover-tablet, covers the feudal lords' tablets, to align tokens of good faith.
translations.idiomatic: The king uses the beveled notch of the cover-tablet to fit over the lords' tablets and align their credentials of good faith.

sentences.zh: 未有臨臣子而執鎮圭者。

translations.literal: There was never one who, facing ministers and subjects, held the tablet of dominion.
translations.idiomatic: No precedent exists for holding the tablet of dominion when facing ministers and subjects.

sentences.zh: 《唐六典》殿中監掌服禦之事，凡大祭祀，則搢大圭，執鎮圭；

translations.literal: The Tang Six Canons: the Director of the Palace Secretariat managed imperial dress; for all great sacrifices, then inserted the great tablet and held the tablet of dominion;
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Six Canons assigns the palace director imperial dress; at great sacrifices he inserted the great tablet and held the tablet of dominion;

sentences.zh: 若大朝會，止進爵。

translations.literal: if a great court assembly, only presented the wine cup.
translations.idiomatic: at grand court assemblies he merely presented the wine cup.

sentences.zh: 《開寶通禮》始著元會執圭，出自西房。

translations.literal: The Kaibao Comprehensive Ritual first recorded holding the tablet at the New Year assembly, emerging from the west chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaibao Comprehensive Ritual first prescribed holding the tablet at the New Year assembly, with the emperor emerging from the west chamber.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，上壽進酒，又令內侍奉圭，於周製、唐禮皆不合。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era, birthday felicitations with wine presentation again had inner attendants present the tablet—all incompatible with Zhou institution and Tang ritual.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunhua, birthday wine rites again had inner attendants hold the tablet—contrary to both Zhou practice and Tang protocol.

sentences.zh: 其元會受朝賀，請不執鎮圭上壽。”

translations.literal: For the New Year assembly receiving congratulations, we ask not to hold the tablet of dominion for birthday felicitations."
translations.idiomatic: For the New Year audience, we ask that the tablet of dominion not be held during birthday felicitations."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔議大圭尺度，詳定所言：“《考工記》：‘鎮圭尺有二寸，天子守之。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict ordered discussion of the great tablet's dimensions; the Detailed Determination Office said: "The Records of Craftsmen: 'The tablet of dominion is one foot two inches; the Son of Heaven keeps it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1080) an edict called for debate on the great tablet's size. The commission cited the Records of Craftsmen: "The tablet of dominion is one foot two inches; the Son of Heaven keeps it."

sentences.zh: ’‘大圭長三尺，杼上終葵首，天子服之’。

translations.literal: ' 'The great tablet is three feet long, tapering upward to a terminal sunflower head; the Son of Heaven wears it.'
translations.idiomatic: 'The great tablet is three feet long, tapering to a sunflower-shaped head; the Son of Heaven wears it.'"

sentences.zh: 後魏以降，以白玉為之，長尺有二寸，西魏以來皆然。

translations.literal: From Later Wei onward, it was made of white jade, one foot two inches long; from Western Wei onward all were so.
translations.idiomatic: From Later Wei it was white jade one foot two inches long—a form unchanged since Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 方而不折，雖非古製，蓋後世以所得之玉，隨宜為之。

translations.literal: Square without bend; although not the ancient make, probably later ages used jade obtained and shaped it as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Square and unbent—not ancient form, but later ages shaped available jade as they could.

sentences.zh: 今請揆玉之有無製之。”

translations.literal: Now we ask to measure whether jade is available and make it.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that it be made according to the jade available."

sentences.zh: 又言：“唐禮，親祀天地神祇，皆搢大圭，執鎮圭。

translations.literal: They further said: "Tang ritual: when the emperor personally sacrificed to Heaven, Earth, and the spirits, all inserted the great tablet and held the tablet of dominion.
translations.idiomatic: They added: "In Tang protocol, when the emperor personally sacrificed to Heaven, Earth, and the spirits, he inserted the great tablet and held the tablet of dominion.

sentences.zh: 有事宗廟，則執鎮圭而已。

translations.literal: When affairs at the ancestral temple, then only held the tablet of dominion.
translations.idiomatic: At the ancestral temple he held only the tablet of dominion.

sentences.zh: 王涇《郊祀錄》曰：‘大圭，質也，事天地之禮質，故執而搢之。

translations.literal: Wang Jing's Record of Suburban Sacrifice says: 'The great tablet is substance; rites to Heaven and Earth are substantive, therefore one holds and inserts it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing's Record of Suburban Sacrifice says the great tablet represents substance, and rites to Heaven and Earth are substantive, so it is both held and inserted in the girdle.

sentences.zh: 鎮圭，文也，宗廟之禮亦文，故無兼執之義。

translations.literal: The tablet of dominion is pattern; ancestral temple rites are also patterned, therefore there is no meaning in holding both.'
translations.idiomatic: The tablet of dominion represents pattern; ancestral rites are patterned too, so there is no reason to hold both.'

sentences.zh: ’不知大圭，天子之笏也，通用於郊廟。

translations.literal: ' They did not know that the great tablet is the Son of Heaven's court tablet, used generally at suburban and temple rites.
translations.idiomatic: They failed to see that the great tablet is the emperor's court tablet, used alike at suburban and temple rites.

sentences.zh: 請自今皇帝親祠郊廟，搢大圭，執鎮圭。

translations.literal: We ask that from now when the emperor personally sacrifices at suburban and temple rites, he insert the great tablet and hold the tablet of dominion.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that hereafter, when the emperor sacrifices personally at suburban and temple rites, he insert the great tablet and hold the tablet of dominion.

sentences.zh: 奉祀之時，既接神再拜，則奠鎮圭為摯，大圭為笏。”

translations.literal: When conducting sacrifice, having received the spirit and bowed twice, then set down the tablet of dominion as offering-gift, the great tablet as court tablet.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving the spirit and bowing twice, the tablet of dominion should be set down as the offering token and the great tablet serve as the court tablet."

sentences.zh: 又言：“《開元》及《開寶通禮》，皇帝升輅，不言執圭。

translations.literal: They further said: "The Kaiyuan Rites and Kaibao Comprehensive Ritual, when the emperor mounts the chariot, do not mention holding the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: They added: "Neither the Kaiyuan Rites nor the Kaibao Comprehensive Ritual has the emperor hold a tablet when mounting the chariot.

sentences.zh: 祀日，質明，至中壝門外，殿中監進大圭，尚衣奉禦，又以鎮圭授殿中監以進。

translations.literal: On the day of sacrifice, at dawn, arriving outside the middle enclosure gate, the palace director advanced the great tablet, the Chief of Imperial Wardrobe presented it to the emperor, and again the tablet of dominion was handed to the palace director to advance.
translations.idiomatic: On sacrifice day at dawn, outside the middle enclosure gate, the palace director brought the great tablet, the Master of Wardrobe presented it, and the tablet of dominion was passed to the director to advance.

sentences.zh: 於是始搢大圭，執鎮圭。

translations.literal: Only then was the great tablet inserted and the tablet of dominion held.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he insert the great tablet and take up the tablet of dominion.

sentences.zh: 今皇帝乘玉輅，執鎮圭，赴景靈宮及太廟、青城，皆乘輅執圭，殊不應禮。

translations.literal: Now the emperor rides the jade chariot, holds the tablet of dominion, proceeding to Jingling Palace, the Grand Temple, and Qingcheng—all mounting the chariot and holding the tablet—is greatly incompatible with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Today the emperor rides the jade chariot holding the tablet of dominion to Jingling Palace, the Grand Temple, and Qingcheng—holding the tablet throughout—which hardly conforms to ritual.

sentences.zh: 請自今乘輅不執圭，還內禦大輦亦如之。”

translations.literal: We ask that from now when mounting the chariot one not hold the tablet; returning within and riding the great palanquin should be likewise.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that hereafter he not hold the tablet while riding the chariot, and the same when returning in the great palanquin."

sentences.zh: 詳定所又言大圭中必之製，請製薦玉繅藉，以木為幹，廣袤如玉，以韋衣之，韋上畫五采文，前後垂之。

translations.literal: The Detailed Determination Office further spoke of the great tablet's center plug design, asking to make the jade-presentation silk mat: using wood as core, width and length like jade, covered with leather; on the leather five-colored patterns painted, hanging front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: The commission also addressed the great tablet's center plug, proposing a jade-presentation mat with a wooden core sized to the jade, leather-covered and painted in five colors, draped front and back.

sentences.zh: 又製約圭繅藉長尺，上玄下絳，為地五采五就，因以為飾。

translations.literal: Also make the tablet-tethering silk mat one foot long, black above and deep-red below, with five-color ground and five bands, thus as ornament.
translations.idiomatic: They also proposed a one-foot tether mat, black above and deep-red below, with five-color ground and five bands as ornament.

sentences.zh: 每奠圭，則以薦玉之繅陳於地，執圭，則以約圭之繅備失墜，因垂之為飾。

translations.literal: Each time the tablet was set down, the jade-presentation silk was spread on the ground; when holding the tablet, the tether silk prevented loss or fall, and thus hung as ornament.
translations.idiomatic: When setting down the tablet the presentation mat was laid on the ground; when holding it the tether mat kept it from slipping and hung as ornament.

sentences.zh: 況大圭搢之紳帶之間，不可無中必，明矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, the great tablet inserted between sash and belt—without a center plug it cannot be, is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly the great tablet inserted in the sash cannot go without a center plug.

sentences.zh: 俟明堂服大圭，宜依鎮圭所約之組，令可係之。

translations.literal: When at the Bright Hall wearing the great tablet, it should follow the cord by which the tablet of dominion is tethered, so it can be tied.
translations.idiomatic: For Bright Hall use the great tablet should have a tether like the tablet of dominion's, so it can be secured.

sentences.zh: 哲宗元祐元年，禮部言：“元豐新禮，皇帝祀天，搢大圭，其製圓首前詘，於禮未合。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou under Emperor Zhezong, the Ministry of Rites said: "The Yuanfeng new rites have the emperor sacrifice to Heaven, inserting the great tablet, its make round-headed and front-curved—incompatible with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 1 (1086) the Ministry of Rites reported: "Under the Yuanfeng rites the emperor's inserted great tablet was round-headed and front-curved, which did not match protocol.

sentences.zh: 今欲仿西魏、隋、唐玉笏之製，方而不折，上下皆博三寸，長尺二寸，其厚以鎮圭為約。”

translations.literal: Now we wish to imitate Western Wei, Sui, and Tang jade court-tablet make: square without bend, top and bottom each three inches wide, one foot two inches long, thickness modeled on the tablet of dominion."
translations.idiomatic: We propose to follow the Western Wei, Sui, and Tang court-tablet form—square and unbent, three inches wide at top and bottom, one foot two inches long, and as thick as the tablet of dominion."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 政和二年，宦者譚稹獻玄圭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe, the eunuch Tan Zhen presented the dark tablet.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 2 (1112) the eunuch Tan Zhen presented a dark jade tablet.

sentences.zh: 其製，兩旁刻十二山，若古山尊，上銳下方。

translations.literal: Its make: both sides carved with twelve mountains, like the ancient mountain vessel, sharp above and square below.
translations.idiomatic: It was carved with twelve mountains on both sides, like the ancient mountain vessel—pointed above and square below.

sentences.zh: 上有雷雨之文，下無彖飾，外黑內赤，中一小好，可容指，其長尺有二寸。

translations.literal: Above were thunder-and-rain patterns; below no trigram ornament; black outside and red within; a small hole in the center fitting a finger; its length one foot two inches.
translations.idiomatic: It bore thunder-and-rain patterns above, no trigram ornament below, black outside and red within, with a finger-sized hole at center, one foot two inches long.

sentences.zh: 詔付廷議。

translations.literal: An edict referred it to court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent it to court for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 議官以為周王執鎮圭，緣飾以四鎮之山，其中有好，為受組之地，其長尺有二寸，周人仿古為之，而王執以鎮四方也。

translations.literal: Deliberating officials held that the Zhou king held the tablet of dominion, its edge ornamented with the mountains of the four quarters; within was a hole as place for receiving the cord; its length one foot two inches; Zhou people imitated antiquity in making it, and the king held it to stabilize the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberators held that the Zhou king's tablet of dominion was edged with the mountains of the four quarters, with a hole for the cord, one foot two inches long—the Zhou replica by which the king symbolically stabilized the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 徽宗乃以是歲冬禦大慶殿受圭焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong then in that year's winter proceeded to the Hall of Great Celebration to receive the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Emperor Huizong received the tablet in the Hall of Great Celebration.

sentences.zh: 三年，又詔曰：“先王以類而求祀，圜丘以象形，蒼玉以象色，冬日以至取其時，大裘而冕法其幽，而未有以體其道，天玄而地黃，今大圭內赤外黑，於以體之，冬祀可搢大圭，執玄圭，永為定制。”

translations.literal: In the third year, another edict said: "Former kings sought sacrifice by analogy: the round altar by form, dark jade by color, winter solstice for the season, great fur robe and coronet following its depth—yet none embodied its Way; Heaven is dark and Earth is yellow; now the great tablet red within and black without, thereby embodying it; winter sacrifice may insert the great tablet and hold the dark tablet—forever as fixed regulation."
translations.idiomatic: A third-year edict declared: "Former kings matched rites by analogy—the round altar by shape, dark jade by color, the winter solstice for season, the great fur robe and coronet for Heaven's depth—yet nothing embodied the Way itself. Heaven is dark, Earth is yellow; the great tablet, red within and black without, now embodies this. Winter rites shall insert the great tablet and hold the dark tablet—a permanent rule."

sentences.zh: 中興仍舊制，大祭祀則執大圭以為笏，上太上皇、皇太后冊寶亦如之。

translations.literal: After the Restoration the old system was kept; at great sacrifices one held the great tablet as court tablet; presenting scrolls and seals to the retired emperor and empress dowager was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynastic restoration the old rule held: at great sacrifices the great tablet served as court tablet, as when presenting scrolls and seals to the retired emperor and empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 皇太子之服。

translations.literal: The crown prince's robes.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's regalia.

sentences.zh: 一曰袞冕，二曰遠遊冠、朱明衣，三曰常服。

translations.literal: First, embroidered robe and coronet; second, distant-travel cap and vermilion-bright garment; third, everyday dress.
translations.idiomatic: First the embroidered robe and coronet; second the distant-travel cap with vermilion-bright dress; third everyday dress.

sentences.zh: 袞冕：青羅表、緋羅紅綾裏、塗金銀鈒花飾，犀簪導，紅絲組，前後白珠九旒，二纊貫水晶珠。

translations.literal: Embroidered robe and coronet: green gauze outer, crimson gauze and red damask lining, gilded silver chased-flower ornament, rhinoceros hairpin guide, red silk cord, front and rear nine white-pearl tassels, two ear-fillers strung with crystal beads.
translations.idiomatic: Embroidered robe and coronet: green gauze outside, crimson gauze and red damask within, gilded silver floral ornament, rhinoceros horn hairpin, red silk cord, nine white-pearl tassels front and rear, and crystal-bead ear fillers.

sentences.zh: 青羅衣，繡山、龍、雉、火、虎蜼五章；

translations.literal: Green gauze upper garment, embroidered with five emblems: mountain, dragon, pheasant, fire, and tiger-moth;
translations.idiomatic: A green gauze upper garment embroidered with five emblems—mountain, dragon, pheasant, fire, and tiger-moth;

sentences.zh: 紅羅裳，繡藻、粉米、黼、黻四章。

translations.literal: Red gauze skirt, four emblems embroidered: algae, grain, axe-fret, and opposed chevrons.
translations.idiomatic: A red gauze skirt with four emblems—algae, grain, axe-fret, and opposed chevrons.

sentences.zh: 紅羅蔽膝，繡山、火二章。

translations.literal: Red gauze knee cover, two emblems embroidered: mountain and fire.
translations.idiomatic: A red gauze knee cover with mountain and fire emblems.

sentences.zh: 白紗中單，青褾、襈、裾。

translations.literal: White gauze inner robe, green cuffs, border, and hem.
translations.idiomatic: White gauze inner robe with green cuffs, border, and hem.

sentences.zh: 革帶，塗金銀鉤䚢，瑜玉雙佩。

translations.literal: Leather belt, gilded silver hook and plaque, paired fine jade pendants.
translations.idiomatic: Leather belt with gilded silver hook and plaque and paired fine jade pendants.

sentences.zh: 四采織成大綬，結二玉環，金塗銀鈒花飾。

translations.literal: Four-color woven great sash, two jade rings knotted, gilded silver chased-flower ornament.
translations.idiomatic: A four-color woven great sash with two jade rings and gilded silver floral ornament.

sentences.zh: 青羅襪帶，紅羅勒帛。

translations.literal: Green gauze sock ties, red gauze girdle.
translations.idiomatic: Green gauze sock ties and a red gauze girdle.

sentences.zh: 玉具劍，金塗銀鈒花，玉鏢首。

translations.literal: Jade-fitted sword, gilded silver chased-flower, jade pommel.
translations.idiomatic: A jade-fitted sword with gilded silver floral mount and jade pommel.

sentences.zh: 白羅襪，朱履，金塗銀釦。

translations.literal: White gauze socks, vermilion shoes, gilded silver clasps.
translations.idiomatic: White gauze socks, vermilion shoes, and gilded silver clasps.

sentences.zh: 從祀則服之。

translations.literal: When accompanying sacrifice, then wore it.
translations.idiomatic: Worn when accompanying sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 遠遊冠：十八梁，青羅表，金塗銀鈒花飾，犀簪導，紅絲組為纓，博山，政和加附蟬。

translations.literal: Distant-travel cap: eighteen ridges, green gauze outer, gilded silver chased-flower ornament, rhinoceros hairpin guide, red silk cord as tassel, sacred mountain ornament; in Zhenghe cicada ornament was added.
translations.idiomatic: Distant-travel cap: eighteen ridges, green gauze outside, gilded silver floral ornament, rhinoceros horn hairpin, red silk tassel, sacred-mountain finial—with cicada ornament added in Zhenghe.

sentences.zh: 朱明服：紅花金條紗衣，紅紗裏，皂褾、襈。

translations.literal: Vermilion-bright dress: red-flower gold-stripe gauze upper garment, red gauze lining, black cuffs and border.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion-bright dress: red floral gold-stripe gauze robe, red gauze lined, black cuffs and border.

sentences.zh: 紅紗裳，紅紗蔽膝，並紅紗裏。

translations.literal: Red gauze skirt, red gauze knee cover, all red gauze lined.
translations.idiomatic: Red gauze skirt and knee cover, both red gauze lined.

sentences.zh: 白花羅中單，皂褾、襈，白羅方心曲領。

translations.literal: White-flower gauze inner robe, black cuffs and border, white gauze square-heart curved collar.
translations.idiomatic: White floral gauze inner robe with black cuffs and border and a white square-heart curved collar.

sentences.zh: 羅襪，黑舄，革帶，劍，佩，綬。

translations.literal: Gauze socks, black shoes, leather belt, sword, pendant, sash.
translations.idiomatic: Gauze socks, black court shoes, leather belt, sword, pendant, and sash.

sentences.zh: 餘同袞服。

translations.literal: The rest same as the embroidered robe set.
translations.idiomatic: The rest matched the embroidered robe regalia.

sentences.zh: 襪帶，勒帛。

translations.literal: Sock ties, girdle.
translations.idiomatic: Sock ties and girdle.

sentences.zh: 執桓圭。

translations.literal: Held the tablet of rank.
translations.idiomatic: He held the tablet of rank.

sentences.zh: 受冊、謁廟、朝會則服之。

translations.literal: Receiving the patent, visiting the temple, and court assembly—then wore it.
translations.idiomatic: Worn when receiving investiture, visiting the temple, or attending court.

sentences.zh: 常服：皂紗折上巾，紫公服，通犀金玉帶。

translations.literal: Everyday dress: black gauze folded-up cap, purple official robe, full rhinoceros-horn and jade-gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: Everyday dress consisted of a black gauze folded-up cap, purple official robe, and a belt of rhinoceros horn, jade, and gold.

sentences.zh: 太宗至道元年，太常禮院言：“南郊，皇太子充亞獻，合著祭祀服。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao under Emperor Taizong, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual Board said: "At the southern suburb, the crown prince serving as secondary offerer should wear sacrificial dress.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's Zhidao 1 (995), the ritual board reported: "At the southern suburban sacrifice the crown prince, serving as secondary offerer, should wear sacrificial regalia.

sentences.zh: 準制度，袞冕以組為纓，色如其綬，青纊充耳，玄衣纁裳，凡九章，每章一行，重以為等，皆織為之。

translations.literal: Per regulations, the embroidered robe and coronet used cord as tassel, color matching the sash; green ear fillers; dark upper robe and vermilion skirt; nine emblems in all, one row per emblem, rank by repetition, all woven.
translations.idiomatic: Per regulation the embroidered robe and coronet had a cord tassel matching the sash color, green ear fillers, a dark upper robe and vermilion skirt, and nine woven emblems in single rows ranked by repetition.

sentences.zh: 白紗中單，黻領，青褾、襈、裾。

translations.literal: White gauze inner robe, chevron collar, green cuffs, border, and hem.
translations.idiomatic: White gauze inner robe with chevron collar and green cuffs, border, and hem.

sentences.zh: 革帶，金鉤䚢。

translations.literal: Leather belt, gold hook and plaque.
translations.idiomatic: Leather belt with gold hook and plaque.

sentences.zh: 大帶，素帶不朱裏，亦紕以朱綠，紐約用組。

translations.literal: Great belt: plain belt without vermilion lining, also edged with vermilion and green, buttons and ties of cord.
translations.idiomatic: The great belt was plain without vermilion lining, edged in vermilion and green, with cord buttons and ties.

sentences.zh: 黻隨裳色，二章。

translations.literal: Chevrons followed skirt color, two emblems.
translations.idiomatic: Chevrons matched the skirt color in two emblems.

sentences.zh: 朱組，雙大綬四采，赤白縹紺，純朱質，長一丈八尺，三百二十首，廣九寸。

translations.literal: Vermilion cord; paired great four-color sashes—red, white, light blue, and dark blue—with pure vermilion ground, one zhang eight chi long, three hundred twenty tassel heads, nine inches wide.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion cord; paired great four-color sashes in red, white, light blue, and dark blue on pure vermilion, one zhang eight chi long, three hundred twenty tassel heads, nine inches wide.

sentences.zh: 小雙綬，長二尺六寸，色同大綬，而首半之，間施二玉環。

translations.literal: Small paired sashes, two chi six cun long, colors same as great sash but half the head width, with two jade rings set between.
translations.idiomatic: Smaller paired sashes were two chi six cun long, matching the great sash colors at half the head width, with two jade rings between.

sentences.zh: 朱襪赤舄，舄加金飾，餘同舊制。

translations.literal: Vermilion socks and red shoes, shoes with gold ornament; the rest same as old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion socks and red shoes with gold shoe ornaments; the rest followed the old system.

sentences.zh: 侍從祭祀及竭廟、加元服、納妃則服之。”

translations.literal: When attending sacrifices, visiting the temple, capping ceremony, or receiving a consort—then wore it."
translations.idiomatic: Worn when attending sacrifices, visiting the temple, at the capping ceremony, or when receiving a consort."

sentences.zh: 詔依上製造。

translations.literal: An edict ordered manufacture according to the above.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered regalia made to these specifications.

sentences.zh: 政和議禮局更上皇太子服製，袞冕惟青纊充耳，餘並同國初之製。

translations.literal: The Zhenghe Commission on Ritual further submitted crown prince dress regulations: only the embroidered robe and coronet had green ear fillers; the rest all matched the founding regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe the ritual commission resubmitted crown prince regalia: only the embroidered robe and coronet used green ear fillers; everything else matched the founding dynasty's forms.

sentences.zh: 加元服、從祀、納妃、釋奠文宣王服之。

translations.literal: Capping ceremony, accompanying sacrifice, receiving consort, and sacrifice to Lord Wen, the Cultural King—wore it.
translations.idiomatic: Worn at the capping ceremony, when accompanying sacrifice, receiving a consort, or offering sacrifice to Confucius as Lord Wen, the Cultural King.

sentences.zh: 中興並同。

translations.literal: After the Restoration, all the same.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynastic restoration the same forms applied.

sentences.zh: 其皇子之服，紹興三十二年十月，禮官言：“皇子鄧、慶、恭三王，遇行事服朝服，則七梁額花冠，貂蟬籠巾，金塗銀立筆，真玉佩，綬，金塗銀革帶，烏皮履。

translations.literal: The imperial princes' dress—in the tenth month of the thirty-second year of Shaoxing, ritual officials said: "The princes of Deng, Qing, and Gong, when attending duties wearing court dress, used the seven-ridge forehead flower coronet, sable-and-cicada frame cap, gilded silver standing brush, true jade pendant, sash, gilded silver leather belt, and black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes' regalia—in Shaoxing 32, tenth month, ritual officials reported: "When Princes Deng, Qing, and Gong performed duties in court dress they wore a seven-ridge forehead flower coronet, sable-and-cicada frame cap, gilded silver standing brush, true jade pendant and sash, gilded silver leather belt, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 若服祭服，則金塗銀八旒冕，真玉佩，綬，緋羅履襪。”

translations.literal: If wearing sacrificial dress, then gilded silver eight-tassel coronet, true jade pendant, sash, and crimson gauze shoes and socks."
translations.idiomatic: For sacrificial dress they wore a gilded silver eight-tassel coronet with true jade pendant and sash, and crimson gauze shoes and socks."

sentences.zh: 詔文思院製造。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Wensi Manufactury to make them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Wensi Manufactury to produce them.

sentences.zh: 後妃之服。

translations.literal: Dress of empresses and consorts.
translations.idiomatic: The regalia of empresses and consorts.

sentences.zh: 一曰禕衣，二曰朱衣，三曰禮衣，四曰鞠衣。

translations.literal: First, the deep ceremonial robe; second, the vermilion robe; third, the ritual robe; fourth, the mulberry robe.
translations.idiomatic: First the deep ceremonial robe; second the vermilion robe; third the ritual robe; fourth the mulberry robe.

sentences.zh: 妃之緣用翟為章，三等。

translations.literal: On consorts' borders pheasants served as emblems, in three grades.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts' robes bore pheasant emblems on the borders in three grades.

sentences.zh: 大帶隨衣色，朱裏，紕其外，上以朱錦，下以綠錦，紐約用青組，革帶以青衣之，白玉雙佩，黑組，雙大綬，小綬三，間施玉環三，青襪、舄，舄加金飾。

translations.literal: The great belt followed robe color, vermilion lined, red edge outside, vermilion brocade above and green brocade below, buttons and ties of green cord; leather belt covered in green; paired white jade pendants; black cord; paired great sashes; three small sashes, with three jade rings set between; green socks and shoes, shoes with gold ornament.
translations.idiomatic: The great belt matched the robe, vermilion lined with red outer edging, vermilion brocade above and green below, green cord fasteners; green-covered leather belt; paired white jade pendants on black cord; paired great sashes and three small sashes with three jade rings between; green socks and shoes with gold ornaments.

sentences.zh: 受冊、朝謁景靈宮服之。

translations.literal: Receiving the patent, court visit to Jingling Palace—wore it.
translations.idiomatic: Worn when receiving investiture or paying court at Jingling Palace.

sentences.zh: 鞠衣，黃羅為之，蔽膝、大帶、革舄隨衣色，餘同禕衣，唯無翟文，親蠶服之。

translations.literal: Mulberry robe, made of yellow gauze; knee cover, great belt, and leather shoes followed robe color; the rest same as the deep ceremonial robe, only without pheasant pattern; worn when personally tending silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: The mulberry robe was yellow gauze; knee cover, great belt, and leather shoes matched the robe; otherwise like the deep ceremonial robe but without pheasant motifs—worn for the empress's silkworm rite.

sentences.zh: 妃首飾花九株，小花同，並兩博鬢，冠飾以九翬、四鳳。

translations.literal: Consorts' head ornaments: nine flower sprays, small flowers the same, both with wide temple wings; coronet ornamented with nine pheasant plumes and four phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts wore nine flower sprays and matching smaller ones, with wide temple wings and coronet ornaments of nine pheasant plumes and four phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 褕翟，青羅繡為搖翟之形，編次於衣，青質，五色九等。

translations.literal: Pheasant robe: green gauze embroidered in swaying-pheasant shape, arranged in rows on the robe; green ground; nine grades in five colors.
translations.idiomatic: The pheasant robe used green gauze embroidered with swaying pheasants in rows on a green ground, in nine five-color grades.

sentences.zh: 素紗中單，黼領，羅縠褾襈，蔽膝隨裳色，以緅為領緣，以搖翟為章，二等。

translations.literal: Plain gauze inner robe, axe-fret collar, gauze damask cuffs and border; knee cover followed skirt color; dark red for collar edge; swaying pheasant as emblem, two grades.
translations.idiomatic: Plain gauze inner robe with axe-fret collar and gauze damask cuffs and border; knee cover matching the skirt, dark-red collar edging, swaying pheasant emblems in two grades.

sentences.zh: 大帶隨衣色，不朱裏，紕其外，餘仿皇后冠服之製，受冊服之。

translations.literal: Great belt followed robe color, no vermilion lining, red edge outside; the rest modeled on the empress's coronet and dress regulations; worn when receiving the patent.
translations.idiomatic: The great belt matched the robe without vermilion lining, red-edged outside; the rest followed the empress's coronet and dress; worn at investiture.

sentences.zh: 皇太子妃首飾花九株，小花同，並兩博鬢。

translations.literal: The crown prince's consort's head ornaments: nine flower sprays, small flowers the same, both with wide temple wings.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's consort wore nine flower sprays and matching smaller ones, with wide temple wings.

sentences.zh: 褕翟，青織為搖翟之形，青質，五色九等。

translations.literal: Pheasant robe: green weave in swaying-pheasant shape; green ground; nine grades in five colors.
translations.idiomatic: Her pheasant robe was green weave in swaying-pheasant form on a green ground, in nine five-color grades.

sentences.zh: 素紗中單，黼領，羅縠褾礻巽，皆以朱色，蔽膝隨裳色，以緅為領緣，以搖翟為章，二等。

translations.literal: Plain gauze inner robe, axe-fret collar, gauze damask cuffs and border—all in vermilion; knee cover followed skirt color; dark red for collar edge; swaying pheasant as emblem, two grades.
translations.idiomatic: Plain gauze inner robe with axe-fret collar and vermilion gauze damask cuffs and border; knee cover matching the skirt, dark-red collar edging, swaying pheasant emblems in two grades.

sentences.zh: 大帶隨衣色，不朱裹，紕其外，上以朱錦，下以綠錦，紐約用青組。

translations.literal: Great belt followed robe color, no vermilion lining, red edge outside; vermilion brocade above and green brocade below; buttons and ties of green cord.
translations.idiomatic: The great belt matched the robe without vermilion lining, red-edged outside, vermilion brocade above and green below, with green cord fasteners.

sentences.zh: 革帶以青衣之，白玉雙佩，純朱雙大綬，章采尺寸與皇太子同。

translations.literal: Leather belt covered in green; paired white jade pendants; pure vermilion paired great sashes; emblem colors and dimensions same as the crown prince's.
translations.idiomatic: Green-covered leather belt, paired white jade pendants, pure vermilion paired great sashes—the emblem colors and dimensions matching the crown prince's.

sentences.zh: 受冊、朝會服之。

translations.literal: Receiving the patent, court assembly—wore it.
translations.idiomatic: Worn when receiving investiture or attending court assembly.

sentences.zh: 鞠衣，黃羅為之，蔽膝、大帶、革帶隨衣色，餘與褕翟同，唯無翟，從蠶服之。

translations.literal: Mulberry robe, made of yellow gauze; knee cover, great belt, and leather belt followed robe color; the rest same as the pheasant robe, only without pheasant; worn when accompanying the silkworm rite.
translations.idiomatic: The mulberry robe was yellow gauze with knee cover, great belt, and leather belt matching the robe; otherwise like the pheasant robe but without pheasant motifs—worn for the silkworm ceremony.

sentences.zh: 中興，仍舊制。

translations.literal: After the Restoration, still the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynastic restoration the old forms remained.

sentences.zh: 其龍鳳花釵冠，大小花二十四株，應乘輿冠梁之數，博鬢，冠飾同皇太后，皇后服之，紹興九年所定也。

translations.literal: The dragon-phoenix flower-pin coronet: large and small flowers twenty-four sprays, matching the number of ridges on the imperial carriage coronet; wide temple wings; coronet ornaments same as the empress dowager's; the empress wore it—fixed in the ninth year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: The empress wore the dragon-phoenix flower-pin coronet—twenty-four large and small flower sprays matching the imperial carriage coronet's ridges, wide temple wings, and ornaments like the empress dowager's—as fixed in Shaoxing 9 (1139).

sentences.zh: 花釵冠，小大花十八株，應皇太子冠梁之數，施兩博鬢，去龍鳳，皇太子妃服之，乾道七年所定也。

translations.literal: Flower-pin coronet: small and large flowers eighteen sprays, matching the crown prince's coronet ridges; two wide temple wings applied; dragon and phoenix removed; the crown prince's consort wore it—fixed in the seventh year of Qiandao.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's consort wore a flower-pin coronet of eighteen flower sprays matching the crown prince's coronet ridges, with two wide temple wings and no dragon-phoenix motifs—as fixed in Qiandao 7 (1171).

sentences.zh: 其服，後惟備禕衣、禮衣，妃備褕翟，凡三等。

translations.literal: Their dress: the empress kept only the deep ceremonial robe and ritual robe; consorts kept the pheasant robe—all three grades.
translations.idiomatic: The empress kept only the deep ceremonial and ritual robes; consorts kept the pheasant robe—in three grades each.

sentences.zh: 其常服，後妃大袖，生色領，長裙，霞帔，玉墜子；

translations.literal: Their everyday dress: empresses and consorts wore wide sleeves, live-color collar, long skirt, cloud stole, and jade pendant drop;
translations.idiomatic: Everyday dress for empresses and consorts was wide sleeves, live-color collar, long skirt, cloud stole, and jade pendant drop;

sentences.zh: 背子、生色領皆用絳羅，蓋與臣下不異。

translations.literal: Outer vest and live-color collar all used deep-red gauze—altogether not different from officials below.
translations.idiomatic: Outer vest and live-color collar were both deep-red gauze—hardly distinct from officials' dress.

sentences.zh: 命婦服。

translations.literal: Dress of ennobled ladies.
translations.idiomatic: The regalia of ennobled ladies.

sentences.zh: 政和議禮局上：花釵冠，皆施兩博鬢，寶鈿飾。

translations.literal: The Zhenghe Commission on Ritual submitted: flower-pin coronet, all with two wide temple wings, precious filigree ornament.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenghe ritual commission specified flower-pin coronets with two wide temple wings and precious filigree ornament.

sentences.zh: 翟衣，青羅繡為翟，編次於衣及裳。

translations.literal: Pheasant robe: green gauze embroidered as pheasant, arranged in rows on robe and skirt.
translations.idiomatic: The pheasant robe used green gauze embroidered with pheasants in rows on robe and skirt.

sentences.zh: 第一品，花釵九株，寶鈿準花數，翟九等；

translations.literal: First rank: flower pins nine sprays, precious filigree matching the flower count, pheasant nine grades;
translations.idiomatic: First rank: nine flower pins, filigree matching the flower count, pheasant in nine grades;

sentences.zh: 第二品，花釵八株，翟八等；

translations.literal: Second rank: flower pins eight sprays, pheasant eight grades;
translations.idiomatic: Second rank: eight flower pins, pheasant in eight grades;

sentences.zh: 第三品，花釵七株，翟七等；

translations.literal: Third rank: flower pins seven sprays, pheasant seven grades;
translations.idiomatic: Third rank: seven flower pins, pheasant in seven grades;

sentences.zh: 第四品，花釵六株，翟六等；

translations.literal: Fourth rank: flower pins six sprays, pheasant six grades;
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank: six flower pins, pheasant in six grades;

sentences.zh: 第五品，花釵五株，翟五等。

translations.literal: Fifth rank: flower pins five sprays, pheasant five grades.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank: five flower pins, pheasant in five grades.

sentences.zh: 並素紗中單，黼領，朱褾、襈，通用羅縠，蔽膝隨裳色，以緅為領緣，加文繡重雉，為章二等。

translations.literal: All with plain gauze inner robe, axe-fret collar, vermilion cuffs and border, gauze damask throughout; knee cover followed skirt color; dark red for collar edge; added patterned embroidery of double pheasants as emblem, two grades.
translations.idiomatic: All had plain gauze inner robes with axe-fret collar, vermilion cuffs and border, and gauze damask throughout; knee covers matching the skirt with dark-red collar edging and double-pheasant embroidered emblems in two grades.

sentences.zh: 〈（二品以下準此。）〉

translations.literal: (Second rank and below follow this.)
translations.idiomatic: (Second rank and below follow this.)

sentences.zh: 大帶，革帶，青襪、舄，佩，綬。

translations.literal: Great belt, leather belt, green socks and shoes, pendant, sash.
translations.idiomatic: Great belt, leather belt, green socks and shoes, pendant, and sash.

sentences.zh: 受冊、從蠶服之。

translations.literal: Receiving the patent, accompanying the silkworm rite—wore it.
translations.idiomatic: Worn when receiving investiture or accompanying the silkworm ceremony.

sentences.zh: 七年，臣僚言：“今文臣九品，殊以三品之服，至於命婦，已厘八等之號，而服製未有名稱。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, officials said: "Now civil officials have nine ranks but only three grades of dress; as for ennobled ladies, eight rank titles have already been established, yet dress forms still lack names.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 7 (1117) officials reported: "Civil officials span nine ranks but only three dress grades; ennobled ladies already have eight rank titles, yet their regalia still lacks formal names.

sentences.zh: 詔有司視其夫之品秩，而定其服飾。”

translations.literal: An edict ordered the responsible offices to look to their husbands' rank and fix their dress and ornament."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the responsible offices to set their dress according to their husbands' rank."

sentences.zh: 詔送禮製局定之。

translations.literal: An edict sent it to the Ritual Regulations Bureau to fix.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the matter to the Ritual Regulations Bureau for determination.

sentences.zh: 其儀闕焉。

translations.literal: The rites were lacking.
translations.idiomatic: The prescribed ceremonial remained incomplete.
